en: "Indeed. The last paradise on Earth, Mirage..."
"There, it's said that during the summer solstice, the sea shines like pearls."
"Did you see it, uncle?"
"Ah. It truly was... a dreamlike sight."
"If I go to that island, can I see it too?"
"...Yes. If we're lucky, surely."
"Then..."
"I'm going too. To Mirage."
"Someday, surely..."
The sky was clear, the sea shimmered blue, and a gentle sea breeze caressed my cheeks.
Captivated by the vivid scenery, my heart raced.
"That is the island I've always dreamed of..."
Aboard the luxury liner heading to the beautiful isolated island of "Mirage," I murmured.
The Strait of the United Kingdom. And the waters of the Republic, sandwiched between the Celtic Sea and the Bay of Biscay—at its westernmost tip.
There is a beautiful island that remains warm year-round and is always in full bloom, perhaps due to the influence of the westerly winds.
A land that, while part of the Republic, belongs to no one— a place that continues to weave its own unique culture.
Its name is Mirage.
The year is 1917, in the midst of a world war.
People hailed this island, far removed from the ravages of war, as “the last paradise on Earth” and cherished it.
#stillreplay_06oth_01
(It’s like a dream…!)
An upscale resort where numerous members of the upper class—including cultural figures, prominent figures, and wealthy individuals—gather.
It is even said that if you go to Mirage, any wish will come true.
And the radiance of the world’s most beautiful ocean—
A mysterious island where you can see “<dic=713> Mail de Loires </dic>’s Pearl” .
(I never imagined I’d actually be “invited” to a place I’ve always dreamed of.)
What’s more, the stay lasts exactly until my birthday—July 12.
(This year’s… 20th birthday is going to be something special.)
With these thoughts in mind, I take an envelope marked out of my bag.
It is this “invitation” that has brought me this far.
――At that moment.
A sudden strong gust of wind blew an envelope out of my hand.
“W-wait!”
I reach out instinctively.
But it doesn’t reach the envelope that flipped in midair.
Just as I thought I’d leap over the deck railing and plunge straight into the sea—
An unfamiliar hand quickly grabbed it.

"Or can you just leave things that bother you alone?"
"…If something bothers me, I want to know."
When I answered honestly, the young man smiled.
"We might get along."
For some reason, his expression looked pleased.
Even though he’s a grown man, I found myself thinking he was just a little bit cute.
“Are you perhaps from the United Kingdom?”
“……Why did you think that?”
"I thought the pronunciation had a slight English accent."
Since I spent some time in the United Kingdom before , I’ll figure it out as soon as I hear a few words.
He blinked rapidly, looking surprised.
“I thought you were a slow learner… But maybe you actually know more than I expected.”
I feel like I was told something rude again.
Maybe it’s better to just accept that this is the kind of person they are.
“I am Evan Crawford. I am a professor at a university in the United Kingdom.”
“……[主人公]・I’m Lapraado. I’m from the Republic.”
He doesn’t look old enough to be a professor, so he might be quite talented.
“Well then, let’s head to the cathedral right away.”
“Huh? W-why is that?”
“Isn’t travel only truly worthwhile when you experience the local culture ?”
“Since we’ve finally met, I’ll give you a little lesson.”
(This person is a little weird……!)
Considering that I might end up living on an island, I’m interested in the local culture.
Thinking it might be interesting to hear his story, I decided to follow him.
Leave the gazebo and return to the front of the cathedral.
Evan walked into the cathedral with a confident stride.
So as not to be left behind, I hurriedly ran after him.
The serene atmosphere drifting through the cathedral takes my breath away.
A gentle ray of sunlight streamed through the vivid blue stained glass, reminiscent of the ocean.
Walking across the marble floor, he says.
“It seems the people of Mirage are baptized in this cathedral within seven days of birth.”
“By doing so, they say the gods promise the islanders bountiful harvests and blessings.”
(If I decide to live on the island, will I also have to go through that initiation?)
Is the large Cronne hanging from the ceiling perhaps something prepared for the festival?
“That’s….”
(A statue of the Virgin Mary? Hmm...)
There appears to be a statue of a goddess on the altar.
In a typical cathedral, a crucifix or Holy Ark would normally be placed in this spot.
“That’s ‘Sirène’… Mirage’s , the goddess of the sea who presides over abundance.”
“There seem to be various legends about her, such as that she once saved the island’s people, but…”
“Now, it’s all in the past. This, too, is nothing more than a decoration for tourists.”
As if reading from a textbook, Evan spoke at length.
You really know your stuff.
Siren, huh...
“You really know your stuff…”
I muttered with awe, and he smiled.
Then, without mentioning my thoughts, he asked.
I'm going to keep looking at the cathedral a bit longer, but what about Ms. Laprade?
Well then... I'll be heading back soon.
I also had a feeling that I wanted to hear more of his explanation, but...
I was tired from the sea voyage and had plans for tomorrow. I just wanted to return to the hotel and rest.
Ms. Laprade. Enjoy the festival.
Yes. Thank you.
But, Sireen... It's about '<dic=320>Seiren</dic>', right?
You know a lot, don't you?
His eyes glittered at my question.
I read a lot of books. And so...
"The sea monster that appears in ancient myths—"
"Its upper body is female. Its lower body is that of a bird, or perhaps a fish. That's the well‑known siren."
"Yes... Yet, is it a god?"
"That's right."
He gave a strong nod to my question.
Standing at the podium as if teaching students, Evan continued his explanation.
"Faith varies greatly depending on the era and the land."
"For example, the 'dragon' in the West refers to a malevolent monster, but..."
"In the East, the 'dragon' is a symbol of the emperor, or even a guardian deity."
Evan, who was explaining, seemed somehow delighted.
He must really love stories that focus on indigenous beliefs.
"Suppose there were gods in this land to begin with. A beautiful woman, who also governs water—"
"Perhaps they came to be called 'Sirènes' due to their affinity with such beings."
"……Do you understand?"
"……A little……."
I nodded weakly, and he smiled more deeply.
"The point is that the god of this land may not have originally been a Sirène, but was perhaps known by a different name."
"It's just a possibility, though."
At his words, I nodded awkwardly.
Just then. He, who had been focused on the story, stumbled over a small step at his feet.
"……I must be tired from walking too much……."
Something suddenly occurs to me, and I speak up.
“Evan, if you don’t mind, could I rest my elbow on yours?”
Evan was staring intently at me, but...
Eventually, she gave a small smile and nodded.
“……Thank you, Miss Lapraud.”
“If you don’t mind, could you help me get to that bench over there for a moment ?”
"Yes!"
Grasping his elbow to support him, I walk slowly, matching his pace.
When he reached the bench, Evan sat down, looking relieved.

en: “You saved me. …I’ve had bad legs for a long time.”
At first, I didn’t notice anything.
But...
Just now, when Evan stumbled, I felt a very slight sense of something being off—
When I looked closely, I noticed that he was dragging one foot .
“It’s okay. You’ll calm down after resting a bit, so don’t look so worried.”
Does it not hurt at all? He’s smiling, and his tone of voice is calm.
“I’m going to stay in this cathedral a little longer. …Why don’t you head home soon?”
“Huh? But—”
“Class is over. As for me, it’s about time I had some personal time.”
He might be saying this so as not to make me worry.
But...
In fact, if I think it might be getting in the way, I can’t really be too pushy about it.
“Are you really sure this is okay?”
“It’s okay. I’ve been with this leg for about 20 years now.”
Evan seems completely unfazed.
“……I understand.”
(I’ll let the Cathedral know just in case……)
I’d like to think this level of meddling is acceptable.
“Ms. Lapraud. Enjoy the festival.”
"Yes. Thank you."
With Evan smiling gently as he saw me off, I left the cathedral alone.
I stroll leisurely down the hill while gazing at the idyllic streets of Ecluse Ville.
As I was gazing, mesmerized by the beautiful sunset where mauve and crimson blended together—
(? Could it be……)
I realized I had started climbing the path and stopped in my tracks.
(Oh, I... I might have gotten a little confused...)
“Vil is located in the interior of the island and adjoins the forest.”
#stillreplay_06oth_04
(It’s totally a forest…!)
(And it's somehow... eerie!)
Startled by an eerie bird call that suddenly echoed through the surroundings, I flinched.
The area was growing darker by the minute.
(I need to hurry back...)
I hurriedly turned on my heel and—
"Kyaa!?"
I tripped over a tree root or something buried in the dirt, nearly falling forward.
I tensed up instinctively, and in the next instant—
"Are you all right, miss?"
A voice came from nearby, and—
I realized someone had pulled me back from falling.
"Ah, thank you so much..."
When I look up, I notice reddish- walnut-colored hair.
My heart is pounding because I almost tripped.
But once I understood my current situation, I started to feel nervous—but for a different reason this time.
I’m firmly supported by those strong arms, and there’s no longer any instability.
Then, looking down at me, he says in a voice that’s surprisingly gentle.
“It’s nothing to thank me for. More importantly, I’m sorry about that, young lady.”
“Huh…?”
“I touched a woman without permission. I wish I could have helped her in a more refined way.”
……He’s a gentleman.
Come to think of it, I feel like there’s just a tiny bit of an English accent in the fluent dialogue.
“Are your legs okay? If you look like you can stand on your own, I’ll let go.”
“If it hurts, I’ll just pick you up like this I’d like to ask for your permission, though…”
“Ah—it’s okay now! Thank you so much…!”
Remembering my current situation, I hurriedly replied, and I repeatedly thanked them.
Was I the one who was weird?
He let out a sigh and let a smile slip.
“……Well, that’s good to hear. Alright, I’ll let you go now.”
The one who helped me was a tall man—one who exuded an air that could almost be described as indolent.
Their vibe is different from that of so-called upper-class people.
“I saw the back of someone heading from the road in Ecluse Ville toward the forest .”
“That’s fine if you’re a local, though…”
“You’re a traveler too, aren’t you? I couldn’t help but chase after you, but I’m glad I made it in time.”
“I see… Thank you very much, that was a big help.”
“I was planning to go back to Fleur d’Or, but before I knew it, I’d gotten lost.”
“Vil’s path is surprisingly complicated, so that’s to be expected.”
He flashed a smile that seemed to suggest he was a people person and, quite naturally, reached out his hand toward me.
“I’m Jack. Jack Lester. I’m here on vacation from the United Kingdom.”
“Nice to meet you, Jack. I am [主人公] Lapraado.”
Introduce yourself and shake hands with Jack.
The reason I was able to take her hand so smoothly, without feeling particularly nervous, was...
Is it because of the unique aura he exudes? Before I knew it, I found myself in his embrace.
“It’s fate that we met here. Let me take you to Fleur d’Or.”
“Eh… Is that okay?”
“Ah. I’m heading back myself anyway. Keep me company on the way.”
“……Yes. Thank you very much!”
I couldn’t help but smile and nod at Jack’s suggestion.
Then, he smiles back at me.
He’s just so good at understanding people’s hearts.
With Jack’s guidance, I was able to safely make my way out to the seaside street.
The sea at dusk is so beautiful— it’s like a painting and truly captivating.
As if reading my mind, Jack spoke up.
“It’s a beautiful island, just as everyone says. The ocean at night must be even better, right?”
“‘The Pearl of Mail D’Loires,’ was it?”
“! I really want to see that ocean…!”
A mysterious night said to be the most beautiful in the world.
I absolutely must see the sight of specks of light rising from the depths of the ocean, swaying with the waves.
“I hear it’s pretty rare to see, but I hope I get a chance to see it while I’m here…”
“Huh… If the young lady’s lucky, maybe things will work out.”
“I’m actually pretty confident in my luck.”
When I nodded back, Jack chuckled to himself, looking amused.
“That’s the best part. I’d like to follow in your footsteps.”
“Is Jack just unlucky?”
“Hmm…”
He raised his gaze slightly and spoke as he gazed at the evening sky.
“Well, I guess it’s neither good nor bad… Coming to Mirage was just a coincidence, after all.”
As I waited for him to continue speaking, Jack glanced briefly in my direction.
“……<dic=907> I won a Bie in a contest run by the </dic> London Times.”
“Huh!? If that’s the case, isn’t that… incredibly lucky …?”
“But if I don’t want that, then the whole thing loses its value, right?”
Saying that, he gave a wry smile, looking a bit flustered.
“It’s well known that prices are high in Mirage, so I was planning to sell off Bie, but…”
“My boss is being a pain… He said, ‘It doesn’t matter whether you’re here or not, so why don’t you take this opportunity to take some time off?’”
Taken at face value, this might sound strict.
But the fact that he’s trying to let me take a break is probably because he cares about me.
“You’re such a kind boss.”
“That’s a mixed blessing…”
Jack said with a sigh, his shoulders slumping as exhaustion seeped through.
“Being the only one in a luxury resort like this during wartime , surrounded by all these rich folks… it just doesn’t feel right…”
We are currently in the midst of the <dic=321> World War </dic>, which began three years ago.
Parts of the Republic have become battlefields, and Paris is occasionally subjected to air raids.
It is well known that the United Kingdom has also been severely affected by food shortages and other issues.
“……Perhaps it’s precisely because of times like these that everyone longs for Mirage even more.”
I think, and continue speaking—
Maybe I just need some time to spend with a smile on my face.
Since I don’t know what will happen tomorrow,
“Maybe we need more time to forget our daily worries and spend our days with a smile.”
Jack fell silent for a moment, as if deep in thought, then gave a slight nod.
“I get the feeling that rich people in every country are always smiling and just having fun all year round…”
“You’re probably right, young lady. It’s important for people to take a break.”
With a gentle smile, he indicated his agreement with my thoughts.
“Since I don’t know what tomorrow will bring, maybe I just want to enjoy the present to the fullest.”
“So, you’re giving up on yourself, is that it?”
Jack narrowed his eyes and stared at me as if trying to confirm the meaning of my words.
His tone was somewhat flat, and I couldn’t quite tell what he was thinking.
“Well, I guess it’s only natural that frustration builds up. It’s just a phase we have to endure.”
Walking along a beautiful promenade while chatting with someone is never boring.
Before I knew it, the Hôtel Azur was beginning to come into view in the distance.
After being dropped off in front of the hotel, I took the opportunity to thank him once again.
“Thank you very much, Jack.”
“Isn’t it a gentleman’s duty to protect a young lady? I was just doing what any gentleman would do.”
He says it with such a deadpan expression that I can’t really tell if he’s serious or joking.
He was the kind of person who could come across as either frivolous or sincere— someone I could never quite figure out until the very end.
Returning to the Hôtel Azur, I look around once more.
I wasn’t in the mood to enjoy the interior earlier, but now that I look at it again, it’s a lovely hotel that looks just like a castle.
Just as I was about to speak to the receptionist, a sudden cheer rang out.
Curious about what on earth was going on, I peeked into the room where I’d heard the sound.
Right after I realized it was apparently a casino.
“――Finn!”
At the sudden, shouting voice, my shoulders jerked involuntarily.
But that voice sounds familiar.
“Don’t pull any silly stunts. Cheating at gambling is something only third-rate people do.”
Sitting at the central table surrounded by a crowd was none other than Leon Vitry, the very same man I had met on board the ship.
I never thought he was the type to raise his voice like that, so I was a little surprised.
“Cheating? All that matters is winning.”
The red-haired young man known as Finn stares down Leon without backing down a single step.
“To that end, any means are acceptable.”
“Isn’t the young president of Vitorie the one who knows that best ?”
Leon fell silent and furrowed his brow for just a moment.
(……Does this seem awkward?)
Just as I thought that, his expression returned to normal.
His poker face is so convincing that I start to wonder if what I saw earlier was just my imagination.
The young man says with a sly grin.
“I wasn’t cheating in the first place.”
“Did you think you could fool me? If so, show me what’s inside that sleeve.”
“Leon, do you really think you’re innocent? Take off that jacket.”
They won’t give an inch to each other.
(Come to think of it, that guy Finn...)
Something about this rings a bell.
Like Leon, he might be a celebrity who appears in the newspaper.
Just then.
(Ah)
By chance, I made eye contact with Leon.
He casually averted his gaze from me and let out a small cough.
"...I shall believe in your proud spirit, Finn."
"The game continues."
Seeing Leon's sudden change in demeanor, Finn furrowed his brow suspiciously.
As they resumed their bet, new cards were dealt into their hands.
"—Bet."
"What will you do? Leon."
He wore a sly smile as he spoke, gauging his opponent's expression.
“That chip, one <dic=108> 10,000 francs </dic>…”
“My hand’s pretty good. Just saying this as a friend, but shouldn’t you fold here?”
“Do you think so?”
Leon wore a confident smile and, without hesitation, flung his hand onto the table.
The five cards that were revealed serve no purpose.
“One card change. With the next card, I’ll make a straight flush.”
The spectators were taken aback and began to murmur in unison.
“……No way, you’re kidding, right? There’s no way something that convenient could happen!”
“That’s right. If you think about it mathematically, my win rate is less than 3%.”
“But that’s enough. It’s a given that I’ll win.”
Without even glancing at the new card dealt to him, Leon placed it face down on the table and said, .
“I’m going all in on this hand.”
At that declaration, the crowd gasped. A wave of commotion spread through the casino.
I am...
Guts
That’s just too reckless……
(They’re really gutsy, aren’t they……)
After all, maybe you can’t become a wealthy person without that kind of resolve.
I’m sure they must be handling sums of money that are beyond imagination on a daily basis to protect the company.
I’m curious about the match results, but it’s already late at night.
Go back to the reception desk and press to have them show you to your room quickly.
(This is just too reckless—I can’t even watch this…!)
Seeing them choose such a hopeless bet, I look away.
And without waiting to see their results, I left the casino and headed back to the reception desk.
Immediately speak to the hotel staff and receive the key.
(This is my room...)
With my heart full of anticipation, I quietly enter the room.
“Wow…!”
I couldn’t help but gasp at the sight of the lovely guest room.
It’s much bigger than the room I’m using in Paris.
I can’t thank Serge enough for setting up such a wonderful place.
Just as I was told earlier today, it seems my package has already been delivered.
On a whim, I take out the invitation.
(I’m sure it was written somewhere…)
My heart is racing, and I feel a strange sense of unease.
I feel like I shouldn’t just leave it as is. I don’t know why, but I just have this feeling.
No matter how hard I try to think, my thoughts won’t come together, and the questions I thought I had are simply fading away like mist.
In the end, no answer was found.

en: A morning greeted after a sound sleep.
The moment I woke up, the room was so luxurious I thought I was still dreaming.
(That's right. I, at the Hôtel Azure ended up staying...!)
Pressing a hand to my racing heart, I got out of the bed, and approached the window.
Outside the window lay the dazzling streets of Mirage and a beautiful sea stretching as far as the eye could see.
Being accommodated in such a lovely room, I could only feel gratitude.
I have an appointment at 2:00 PM today at the island's administrative office—Portail Bleu.
It is a place I have never been before. I want to arrive with plenty of time to spare.
After getting ready, I left the hotel and entered a café that had been on my mind.
It was a shop I had noticed yesterday while Serge was guiding me on the way to Ville.
Its charming appearance had caught my eye and left a lasting impression.
I would enjoy a meal serving as both breakfast and lunch, and then savor a post-meal coffee leisurely—
After that, if I head to the administrative office, the timing would be just right.
(What should I eat?)
Thinking back, I had fallen asleep yesterday without even having dinner.
I had resolved to eat my fill today, and was looking over the menu when—
“Hey, you?”
“Huh?”
A well-dressed woman sitting next to me speaks to me.
“If you’d like, would you like to grab a bite to eat with me here?”
“Huh?”
Looking over, their table is piled high with food.
Tomato soup packed with fresh seafood, served with salmon and cheese tartine.
Seasonal fruit salad, pain au chocolat. Even sugar-coated baked apples.
(That looks delicious……)
“I guess I asked for too much, thinking I was still young. Even though the kids aren’t with me this time…”
“Hey, you… You’re a nuisance, aren’t you?”
The sight of the shy wife and her husband with a troubled expression really conveys how close they are.
“Is this no good? I thought you’d help me Could you come with me…?”
Hearing my wife’s pleading words, I—
Is that okay?
Is this a bother...?
“Is that okay? I’m so happy!”
“Really? That’s great…!”
“Sorry about that, Mademoiselle….”
The couple is smiling happily.
It’s great to be able to eat delicious food, and if I can help people at the same time, that’s even better.
“But isn’t this a bother for you…?”
“That’s not true! As you can see, I haven’t even started cooking yet.”
“Of course I’ll share it with you… right?”
“Hehe…”
Overwhelmed by the gentle yet forceful energy of my wife, I can’t help but laugh.
“Understood. I’ll go ahead and get started.”
“Sorry about that—I was a bit pushy…”
Even as he said that, my husband gave a wry smile, looking somewhat relieved.
They said their children had recently left home, and they had come on this trip just the two of them.
“I’m so happy to have made friends on my travels”—
My wife, who laughed so cheerfully, was much older than me, but she was very endearing.
Even though I was trying to be polite, they went out of their way to order coffee and snacks for me as well...
I feel so bad— —that I’m almost sorry to be treated so well.
I spent time with them, feeling grateful for the good fortune of having met such a wonderful couple.
As I approached Ecruse Ville, I heard the laughter of innocent children.
Looking at it, it looks like they’re playing soccer.
I couldn’t help but squint at the heartwarming scene.
“If you turn here, you’ll reach the cathedral…”
“……Well, maybe this one?”
Along the way, I asked the islanders for directions as I headed toward our meeting place—the Bureau.
"So this is Polteille Blue..."
Its pristine white facade, set against the sea, felt less like a government office and more like an art museum.
Calculating backwards from when I left the café, it should be almost time for our appointment.
But...
(...Is Serge not here yet...)
Perhaps the hotel manager is busy. I looked back down the path, but there was no sign of him.
(I should go in ahead and explain the situation)
I was hesitant to be late without even sending a message.
Feeling a bit nervous, I stepped into the Bureau.
It was a beautiful building made of marble, resembling a museum or gallery.
"Ah, are you Miss Aria?"
“Oh, are you from the Lapraud family?”
The person at the reception desk was a kind-looking young man.
“You came to see the Director about Grandma, didn’t you?”
“Yes. [主人公]・I’m Lapraado. Nice to meet you.”
“Actually, I was supposed to come here with Serge Glack… ”
Whenever I say that, he looks troubled.
“Ah… Let’s just leave it be.”
“Huh?”
“That’s just the kind of person he is.”
“What!?”
As I was wondering if that approach was really okay, he introduced himself.
“Oh, I haven’t introduced myself yet, have I? I’m Yuris. Yuris Blanchard.”
“I’m technically listed as the Deputy Director of the Administration Bureau.”
(Oh, really…!)
He’s probably not even 30 yet.
I never would have imagined—until I was told—that he was the second-in-command of the organization that manages the island.
“For now, I’ll show you to the Director’s office. This way, please.”
“Y-yes!”
As we walk down the hallway, Yuris strikes up a friendly conversation with us.
“Aria, have you heard yet about what kind of organization the Administration Bureau is ?”
“[主人公]-chan, have you already heard about what kind of organization the Administration Bureau is ?”
“Oh, yes. I’m in charge of managing the island —from Serge.”
“Asset management, maintaining public order… Oh, and you’re also doing marine research, right?”
“That’s right. You see, unlike the mainland , there aren’t any police on this island, are there?”
“So I’m doing my best with patrols and stuff, too. There’s always a lot going on during the festival period, after all…”
“……What do you mean, ‘various things’?”
When I asked, Yuris looked at me as if startled.
“……Well, you know. When it comes to festivals , everyone gets really excited, right?”
“Oh, that’s right.”
I nodded slightly in response, realizing that this might lead to some commotion or conflict.
“Especially since there’s a rumor that at the Mirage Festival, any wish will come true.”
“There are actually tourists who take it at face value every year.”
The Summer Solstice Festival lasts for three whole weeks...
It certainly makes you feel like it wouldn’t be strange if something unusual were to happen.
Where the elevator dropped me off—the room that Yuris had shown me to was empty.
“Huh. That’s unusual—they’re not here…”
“I’m going to look for it, so could you wait for me? Oh, and feel free to look around the room as much as you like.”
Seeing me inadvertently show my unease, Yuris smiled brightly and said,
“It’s okay. I don’t leave anything lying around that I’d be embarrassed for anyone to see.”
I was left alone in the director’s office.
(The bureau chief who was an acquaintance of my grandmother...)
(I wonder if he's actually my grandfather after all?)
Even as my thoughts drift aimlessly, my gaze suddenly turns toward the window outside —
(...Is that the sea?)
It was a scene that seemed unreal.
It seems this building exists within the sea.
(Beautiful...)
…Whenever I look at the sea, I always feel a sense of dread somewhere in my heart .
But the sea trapped behind the glass cannot reach this side.
Because I can feel safe, I was simply drawn to its azure beauty.
#stillreplay_06oth_03
I cautiously move toward the window at the far end.
He gently reached out his fingertip toward the glass—and in the very next instant.
“What are you doing in my room?”
――Suddenly, my wrist was grabbed with great force.
She has such delicate features that she could easily be mistaken for a young girl.
In contrast, he is taller than me, and his grip on my wrist is relentless.
“Ah, um….”
Glaring at me as I stood there bewildered, he said.
“What were you trying to do just now?”
Grilled in a harsh tone, I—
I tried to look at the ocean
Who are you?
“I was trying to look at the ocean…”
“Why?”
Both the short, questioning tone and the stern gaze make me feel terribly uncomfortable, as if I’m being suspected.
“……It was beautiful, so……”
The young man said nothing, but his piercing gaze seemed to be observing me.
But a few seconds later, he silently released my hand.
“Who are you…?”
To suddenly have my hand grabbed from behind and be sternly questioned like this—
Confused as to why this situation had arisen, I asked him in return.
Perhaps my reaction was unexpected, for the young man’s expression twisted into one of confusion.
“I’m the one asking, aren’t I?”
“……I didn’t do anything in particular, so I have nothing to say.”
I sensed a hint of wariness in the way they looked at each other.
As they continued to gaze at each other like that for a moment—
Eventually, the young man let go of my hand without saying a word.
“……I’m Rudy Rochefort. I’m the director here.”
Even more so than Yuris, who told me he was the deputy director, he looks young.
In fact, not much different from me.
“……I’m sorry for barging in like this.”
“Mr. Yuris guided me—”
“What you should be apologizing for is making that arbitrary decision, right?”
“I’m not blaming you for coming in. I’d heard from Yuris that you were coming.”

“Rudy. Whether or not to use the permanent residency is up to her to decide.”

"Wait, my princess."
He called out to me in a gentle voice.
"I rescued you when you were in trouble. Surely I deserve a little reward?"
"...Well, I'm sorry, but I don't really have anything to give you—"
Before I could finish my sentence.
He made a dashing—slightly old-fashioned—gesture, flicking his fingers side to side with a "chic-chic" sound.
"My adorable mademoiselle. Let's have a <dic=902>rendezvous</dic> with me for the rest of the day."
Charles smiled as he watched me, who was taken aback—
Rudy held the silver cup— the ceremonial Holy Grail—high, pointing it toward the starry sky.
“O God. We shall offer our prayers on the night of the summer solstice.”
Next, a seashell, wheat, herbs, and other items are placed into the Holy Grail in the following order: .
Just as I thought the cup had been placed on the tabletop where the flame of the prepared candle flickered .
(! When did that happen…?)
What Rudy held in his hand was a slender sword that glowed in the light of the lantern.
Flipping his dark cloak and raising his sword— his figure was reminiscent of a knight from a fairy tale.
“O our God. For the blessings bestowed by the sea, your children kneel.”
The rapier is swung in a cross-like motion.
It was a ceremony vastly different from the church Masses I had attended up to that point.
(Somehow, it made my heart feel warm...)
A strange sense of unease makes me tilt my head involuntarily.
(Or is it just my imagination…?)
“That” is something far too special.
Detection via magic is virtually impossible.
A terrifying backlash strikes the caster who touches what must not be touched.
Therefore――
To disperse the magical power of “that thing” flowing in here, I split myself in advance.
In other words, a part of oneself… Prepare a Holy Grail filled with your own blood, and use it as a decoy.
Prepared for this day: Legacy of the Ancient Capital—I hold my hand up to the clouded mirror.
――I see it――
(……Hope lies over there――)
After watching the ceremony at the cathedral――
I returned to the hotel without incident , slept soundly, and woke up feeling refreshed.
Just as I got off the elevator, the manager of this Hôtel Azur—
I spotted Serge.
“Good morning, Serge.”
“Yes, good morning. Did you sleep well last night?”
I nodded vigorously.
It was the first time in my life that I’d slept on such a fluffy bed.
“That’s good to hear. If you’d like breakfast now, I’ll show you to the restaurant.”
“! Please do this.”
Serge pulls out a chair with a respectful gesture and invites you to sit down.
“Thank you…!”
“No, no. What would you like to drink?”
“<dic=314> Chocolat Chaud </dic>—do you have any?”
Of course. I'll bring it right away.
Just after Serge stepped away from my seat, someone approached, as if swapping places.
Good morning, Aria.
Good morning, [主人公].
Good morning, Leon.
If it's alright, is this spot okay?
He points to the seat across from me.
I was a little surprised, but—
“……Of course. Here you go.”
“If you’d like, would you like to grab a bite to eat with me here?”
I still vividly remember how much fun it was sharing a table with strangers while traveling.
(When I think the other person is the CEO of a big company, I get nervous, though...)
Leon asks while seated.
“Did you go see yesterday’s ceremony, too?”
“Yes. It was mysterious and somehow moving.”
“I’m glad you enjoyed it. …Actually, I’ve been looking for you.”
“Huh? Why is that?”
“Up until we left the hotel, we were practically in sync, weren’t we?”
“I thought, ‘Since we’re going anyway, let’s go together…’ But I lost sight of them in the crowd.”
“I’m sorry. I didn’t notice at all…!”
Just as I was frantically apologizing, Serge returned.
“Sorry to keep you waiting. This is Chocolat Chao.”
Chocolate with a sweet aroma is poured into a ceramic bowl.
“……It’s leaking.”
“Oh.”
Serge’s eyes widened.
“My apologies. I’ll bring you a new one right away.”
“No, I’m fine!”
Sure, there are a few minor overspills, but they’re nothing more than a quick wipe with .
“I’m sorry… I’m just clumsy—I’m so embarrassed.”
“……It’s a good thing she was a decent customer. What did you do before you started working at the hotel?”
“About a year ago, I was working at the Administration Bureau.”
“Huh!?”
I was taken aback at first, but come to think of it...
“It seems Mr. Rudy has disliked me for quite some time now.”
It seems he’s known Rudy for a long time— I realize that might be the reason.
“Lord Vitorie. What would you like to drink?”
“Coffee, please.”
"Understood."
Serge bowed politely and left our table.
“Um, Leon. Where did you realize that Serge had a previous job?”
“Is it because I spilled some chocolate…?”
Wondering if that alone would be enough to figure it out, I’ll ask a question.
Then, he gave a wry smile.
“I can’t really tell just from that. But….”
“I heard that the manager at Azur changed last year .”
“? …A message for Leon?”
“Ah, yeah. This is a hotel funded by multiple investors .”
“Vitry Corporation is among them, you know.”
(Oh, really...!)
Dinner with Leon turned out to be more relaxed and enjoyable than I had initially imagined, and we were able to chat comfortably.
After dinner, I stepped outside the hotel and was once again overwhelmed by the island’s dazzling scenery.
(What should I do today?)
(Oh, maybe I’ll go see the art exhibition?)
Earlier, there were people at the restaurant who brought up that topic .
Works of art by artists, such as paintings and sculptures, as well as jewelry made with rare gemstones and precious metals.
It seems that items favored by the upper class are on display at the Fleur d’Or Gallery .
(I probably can’t afford to buy it, but I think I could at least pay the admission fee…!)
Stepping out onto the bustling, vibrant street teeming with tourists, I walked around, looking around.
(That’s...)
I could see Rudy in the distance.
I slept soundly on the soft bed and woke up to a new morning.
When I wake up, the first thing I remember is last night.
(It was a mysterious ritual...)
Perhaps it’s because of the setting—the cathedral at night.
It really sticks with me.
(……Come to think of it)
“Isn’t travel only truly worthwhile when you experience the local culture ?”
“Faith varies greatly depending on the era and region, after all.”
(About this island……)
(I’d like to learn more about this, too.)
I had breakfast at the hotel restaurant.
I was a little nervous in such a luxurious setting, but the food was delicious, and I had a great time.
As I step into the reception area, I spot him.
“Good morning, Evan.”
“Good morning. So you were staying at the Hôtel Azur too, weren’t you?”
“Are you heading out sightseeing or something?”
"Yes."
"Where to?"
Just like when we first met yesterday.
Evan knows no such thing as restraint and pushes his way in relentlessly.
“I haven’t decided on a specific location yet.”
“It’s just that yesterday’s ceremony was so magical, I thought it was wonderful…”
“I’ve become curious to learn more about this island’s culture and things like that.”
“I see. So what you’re trying to demonstrate is a proactive attitude stemming from intellectual curiosity, isn’t it?”
Evan smiled contentedly.
"Would you like to go with me? I'm about to head out on fieldwork."
"I intend to travel around the island to study the Mirage legends."
"…Is that okay?"
When I asked apologetically, he nodded.
"Maybe it's a professional hazard. Kids with a thirst for knowledge are already appealing to me. I just want to nurture them."
"Thank you so much…! Then, please let me join you."
If I accompany Evan, who knows the island well, there will be much to learn.
When I expressed my gratitude, he nodded cheerfully.
Evan left the inn—
He took me to the administration office.
"Hm… This year, on top of everything, we’ve got troublesome travelers…"
Ulysse lets out a wry laugh, looking utterly exasperated, but Evan remains unshaken.
"I don't think we're making this any harder than it needs to be... We simply want to learn about the island's history."
"It would be quite improper to dismiss such pure intentions, wouldn't you agree?"
There was no pressure in his tone.
He was simply weaving words straight from his heart.
"I've heard that Portail Bleu conducts marine research in the Iroise Sea..."
"There must be some publicly available materials, right?"
"I believe asking to see them is a perfectly reasonable request."
"In the outside world, that's just how things are done, I suppose. I've never heard of it on our island."
"Ah, um, Evan..."
Wasn't this a bit too forceful?
Just as I tugged at his sleeve to stop him.
“Well, sure, I’ve definitely released some of it.”
I’m taken aback by the unexpected response.
“I-Is that so…?”
“I never said I wouldn’t show you.”
“It’s just that this person kept talking nonstop by themselves —I didn’t have a chance to get a word in.”
He shrugged and said to Evan.
“The Administration Bureau’s library is open to the public. You’re free to look at anything you like there.”
“That’s great. Thank you!”
“No, no. …Oh, taking books out of here is prohibited, you know.”
“Put what you’ve read back where you found it. Please be thorough about this.”
“…………………… I’ll do my best.”
After a long pause, Evan replied with a smile, but...
(Ah—)
I had a hunch.
(Evan is probably not the type of person who’s very good at tidying up or anything like that…!)
Since I knew someone who used to stack books to cause avalanches, it was easy to imagine.
Yuris led us to the library on the second floor of Portail Bleu.
“……Considering the size of the island, it seems to be quite well-equipped.”
“The fact that I can’t see any other players at all is a bit concerning, though…”
“Is that so? It doesn’t seem strange to me at all.”
“I mean, no one in their right mind would come all the way to Mirage just to look at the Administration Bureau’s library.”
“……Now that you mention it, maybe you’re right……”
Even if, in between sightseeing, you feel like reading a book ...
The bookstore at Fleur d’Or is all you need.
No one in their right mind would come all the way here in search of a library whose very existence is uncertain.
“Even staff members rarely use it, so we don’t have a librarian on staff.”
“I do clean it regularly, but I think there might still be some dust or spots I can’t quite reach.”
“Well, just think of it as the weight of history and give it a rest.”
Before I could finish speaking, without waiting for my reaction—
“Well then, I’m going back to work.”
Yuris left us behind and walked out of the library.
“Um…”
When I turned my gaze to the side, there was no one there.
Before I knew it, Evan had already reached toward the bookshelf and was pulling out several promising books.
“Where should I start checking?”
When I spoke to him, Evan replied with a voice brimming with anticipation.
“I won’t put them in any particular order. After all, I don’t even know what kind of materials are available yet.”
“First, the island’s history, geography, and structure… Pick up those fragments one by one.”
“Reconstruct the island’s outline from multiple perspectives and synthesize it into a form that can be viewed from above.”
It seems like I understand, but I’m not quite sure.
“……Um, is there anything I can help you with?”
“For starters, you should just read as many books as you can get your hands on. Getting a handle on what’s here is the first step, I guess.”
"Got it."
Since it’s called “fieldwork,” I thought I’d be walking around town more.
Come to think of it, since I’ve already arrived “on-site” …
It might be reasonable to set our sights on the Administration Office—which likely holds the most resources on this island.
“Ms. Lapraud. You’re my assistant today. I’m counting on you to work hard.”
"Yes!"
Then—
We looked through more than a dozen books.
The books on this island are written in the language of the Republic.
It seems Evan occasionally comes across unfamiliar words , and he asked me a few questions.
Conversely, if the text becomes too academic, I’ll switch to asking questions.
“……This Mirage has quite an interesting history, doesn’t it?”
He stopped turning the pages and narrowed his eyes.
“In 1663, this island was designated as a quarantine station for the Port of Brest.”
“That was right around the same time a permanent quarantine station was established in Marseille.”
“And… the year 1666, a year of wonders. The Great Plague made no exception for this island.”
“! The Black Death……”
There’s probably no one who doesn’t know that name.
Even today, it remains a terrifying disease with no known cure.
“It seems that the festival in Mirage took on its current form around this time, too.”
“During a plague, you say?”
“That’s right. When people find themselves in dire straits, they pray to God, and when their situation improves, they give thanks for their salvation….”
Evan gave a small, wry smile.
“……There’s no way to prove that it’s really thanks to God, though.”
“Anyway, when you feel God’s grace or a miracle, that’s when rituals and faith begin to flourish.”
“A blessing……”
Serge did say that, indeed.
“This is a ritual to give thanks to the Sea God, who protects this island and bestows blessings upon its inhabitants.”
At that moment, Evan muttered casually.
“……Well, in Mirage’s case, that belief might not just be a mere delusion, though.”
“What do you mean?”
“There’s a legend that during the festival, a special—so-called ‘magic book’—appears on this island.”
“They say if you collect three of those, your wish will come true.”
“Wow…! That’s wonderful.”
“From a mythological perspective, I feel this could be considered the lost treasure of Is, which sank into the sea.”
A city sunk beneath the sea and a book that grants any wish.
The more I hear about it, the more this island seems just like the setting of a fairy tale.
What made it even more interesting was that there was an academic basis for it, and I listened intently without getting bored.
"Miss Laprade."
"Yes."
"You're going to watch the ritual too, right? Then come with me."
"Yes. Understood."
(...What?)
I noticed the anomaly as we reached the outskirts of Écrouze-Ville.
Before I knew it, Evan was nowhere to be seen.
(Could it be that...)
Did he turn back at the last corner and head the other way?
I retraced my steps and headed toward the forest.
As if inviting me, a strange melody drifted from deep within the woods.
"Is someone ahead of me...?"
Emerging from among the trees was what must once have been a church—a desolate ruin.
……A strange sound can be heard coming from inside.
I reached out and touched the door myself.
――Sound stops.
The abandoned, silent cathedral was, for some reason, extremely eerie.
At that moment.
Starlight streaming through the clouds illuminates the cathedral.
“Huh…!”
A strained scream escaped her lips.
In the center of the cathedral, a vast number of people lie piled on top of one another.
It looks like some kind of tacky decorative object.
Someone who had breathed their last with an expression of agony is now scratching their throat with blackened fingertips.
Below that lies someone’s charred hand.
A body with limbs bent in strange directions , like a doll’s.
“Ah, ah……”
Only the sea of blood spreading across the floor feels unnaturally vivid.
Faced with this terrifying sight, my legs won’t move.
I was desperately trying to hold back my nausea.
The blood flowing down touched the tips of my shoes, and a squelchy, unpleasant sensation spread through me.
“Hmm…!”
I instinctively closed my eyes.
And then, tentatively, I opened my eyes again...
“Huh…?”
There was nothing there.
There are no piled-up corpses, nor is there any blood staining the floor.
Surprise quickly turns to fear and anxiety.
What on earth did I just see?
That scene was so vivid down to the finest details that I couldn’t believe it was just a hallucination.
“……Is anyone there……?”
She calls out in a trembling voice.
I came here because I remembered why I was here.
(What on earth is that strange sound……)
At that moment.
The floor creaked.
A figure slowly emerges from the depths of the abandoned church.
And there, illuminated by the starlight peeking through the cathedral’s windows , was the figure—
I jumped out of bed without thinking.
That was a familiar hotel room.
I was apparently lying on the bed, still in my clothes.
"…then…."
"Was that just a dream…?"
In a hurry, I straightened my appearance, fled the room, and as I descended to the reception—
The hotel manager, Serge, called out to me.
“Ah, Aria. How are you feeling?”
“Ah, [主人公]. How are you feeling?”
“Ah, yes… I’m feeling fine…”
Seeing how he looked somewhat worried, I replied, feeling a bit confused.
Then, Serge gives a gentle smile.
“That’s good to hear. I’m relieved. I was really surprised yesterday…”
“Yesterday… Did anything happen?”
“Ah… So, you really don’t remember, do you?”
Feeling nervous at the cryptic question, I nod.
“Y-yes. I just found myself in the room.”
“I remember up to the point where I was about to go watch the festival ceremony, but…”
“You didn’t go to watch the ceremony. Because you suddenly collapsed just as the evening party was ending.”
“What!?”
I couldn’t help but gasp at the shocking truth.
“Maybe the fatigue from the voyage is catching up with you. Have you been drinking too much, perhaps?”
“Oh, I don’t remember that…!”
“I did have a doctor take a look, but the diagnosis was that he seems to be sleeping soundly.”
“H-Have I caused you that much trouble?”
“I’m so sorry…!”
When I apologized nervously, Serge smiled.
“Anyone can get sick. Anyway, since there didn’t seem to be any problems, last night I had them carry me straight to my room….”
“Huh? Um, did the doctor carry me …?”
“Oh, no, no. When you fainted and were about to fall, someone who happened to be nearby caught you.”
“That person stayed right here with you the whole time while I went to get a doctor.”
“He ended up carrying it all the way to my room. Oh, I unlocked the door myself.”
“Ah, thank you… But….”
“Besides Mr. Serge and the doctor, is there anyone else who’s helped me so much…?”
I’ve caused so much trouble that I felt a momentary dizzy spell.
“I’d really like to thank you, but I don’t know who you are… ”
“Yes. I figured you’d say that, so I made sure to ask for your name and contact information .”
He hands over the note with a smile.
“Thank you…!”
When I checked the note, it contained the name of a hotel that appeared to be his place of stay, and—
The name “Jack Lester” was written there.
(Come to think of it……)
“I’m Jack. Jack Lester. I’m here on vacation from the United Kingdom.”
“Hey, hey! Are you okay, young lady!?”
In my faint memories, I feel like I heard that voice.
(Jack helped me…!)
That day. After finishing breakfast at the hotel.
I set out into the city to find him and thank Jack—
I wonder if the crowd made me a bit tipsy.
Feeling my chest stir for no particular reason—
I couldn't leave the spot until the ceremony announcing the start of the festivities was over .
On the way back from the cathedral.
I avoid the crowded main street and walk along the seaside promenade while feeling the sea breeze.
Even though it's so beautiful in the daytime, the night sea is pitch black and a little eerie.
"…Hey, Aria."
"…Hey, [主人公]."
A voice suddenly calls out to me.
Surprisingly, the voice that seemed to come from right nearby makes my heart race as I turn around…
There, a familiar child stood.
"…Ahès?"
Come to think of it, before the ritual began—
I remember seeing her.
"…Why are you here? Ahès, you're a child of the Portail Bleu…"
If she were returning to the Administration, she shouldn't be taking this path.
Considering that the ritual was scheduled to begin around midnight…
It is very worrying to see a small child out alone at this hour.
"Did you get separated from the others? Shall we go back to the Administration together?"
Feeling a bit flustered inside, I called out to her.
She stared at me intently and said.
"Aria, was kind to me."
"[主人公], was kind to me."
“I like you, Aria…”
“I like [主人公]…”
“……Thank you?”
I couldn’t help but tilt my head.
……Ahès gave a small smile.
“I’ll tell you just a little bit.”
“If things keep going like this, Aria will die, I guess. …Because it’s sad….”
“If things keep going like this, [主人公] will die, I guess. …It’s so sad…”
(Am I... going to die...?)
It sounded like a completely out-of-the-blue remark.
Yet, I couldn’t just laugh it off as a joke—
Silently, like water seeping in, a sense of unease spreads through my heart.
“……What does that mean?”
“Aria, listen carefully.”
“[主人公], listen carefully.”
“You are about to fight.”
“To survive, you have to take from others.”
“To take…?”
(……What?)
“It’s already started.”
“Even if you don’t know anything…”
Ahès’s hand slowly rises and points at my chest.
“……Everyone is after ‘it,’ you know.”
“That…?”
She nodded slightly.
And at the same time――
Right in front of my chest, a dazzling flash of light appeared.
Squinting against the glare, I unconsciously reached out my hand…
A single book that had appeared there now lay in the palm of my hand.
“……That book……”
“Huh?”
Suddenly, a voice is heard from behind.
As I turned around, still holding the book, there stood Leon.
……And at the same time, the weight in my hand vanishes.
As you can see, I have nothing.
On the contrary—
“……Ahès?”
This road has a clear view. Yet...
The woman who had been right before my eyes just moments ago had suddenly vanished.
"...Are you okay, Aria?"
"...Are you okay, [主人公]?"
I, confused by the string of eerie events, am called by Leon.
"You don't look well. The sea breeze must have chilled you a little?"
“No matter how much of a mirage it is, no matter how close it is to the summer solstice, it really does get chilly late at night.”
“Maybe it’s about time we headed back to the hotel. I’m on my way home anyway, so let’s go together—”
“B-but, Ahès is….”
“Ahès?”
“Y-yes… There was a girl here just a moment ago, right?”
Leon furrowed his brow in puzzlement.
“I’ve been watching you for a while now, but…”
“You’ve always been alone, haven’t you? There was no one else.”
“Huh!?”
“She was talking to herself by the sea, so I was worried about what was wrong.”
“Just as I was about to ask if something was wrong, you happened to turn around.”
“N-no way….”
What Leon saw was very different from my perception.
“I—I was just talking to a kid from this island a moment ago…”
“Since it’s already this late, I was thinking of giving you a ride to the Administration Office.”
“Before I knew it, they were gone…”
“Hmm…”
“……<dic=611>Voodoo</dic>, maybe?”
He gives an ambiguous, wry smile.
They’re not taking this seriously at all.
“I-it’s true! I’m not joking…”
“By the way, you. You had that mysterious book, didn’t you? It seems… you don’t have it anymore, though.”
I felt just a little relieved, wondering if Leon had seen the book too.
“Y-yes, that’s right. That book, all of a sudden….”
“……It appeared right in front of me……”
Why does it sound more and more like a lie the more I talk?
Unfortunately, even I couldn’t find my own words convincing.
“There’s something about the book that’s been on my mind. Could you spare a little time tomorrow?”
Surprised by the sudden offer, I reply.
“……That’s fine, I guess……”
“Would this afternoon work?”
“Why?”
“I’m worried about whether that girl made it home, so tomorrow I’ll head to Portail Bleu first.”
If we are to believe Leon’s testimony—
To begin with, Ahès wasn’t even here.
Though the very fact that I spoke with her might just be my illusion.
“Hmm…”
He tilted his head as if puzzled.
“Hey, I should go first, right?”
“I wouldn’t go so far as to say it’s meaningless—but…”
“Are you deliberately making me wait just to check something that doesn’t seem necessary…?”
In a tone that suggested he was struggling to understand, he asked me back, looking puzzled.
“I’m Leon. Leon Vitry. It’s nice to meet you, Aria.”
“I’m Leon. Leon Vitry. It’s nice to meet you, [主人公].”
The Leon I’ve come to know is—
He was gentle and never acted superior; he must have been a wonderful, prince-like person.
“Huh? Huh……?”
I was convinced that he would gladly nod in agreement.
I can’t hide my shock at the reaction, which is so different from what I expected.
“As you know, I’m backed by Vitry, one of the world’s leading corporations with influence on a national scale.”
“Even here, where I came to take a vacation, I’m busy enough to have business meetings and evening events I can’t miss.”
“And yet, even though I told you I’d make time for you tomorrow… ”
It was Leon who said he wanted to talk.
And yet, I feel like I’m getting a reaction as if I were the one begging for it…
(W-Wait, is something wrong with me…?)
Looking at me, who was confused, Leon said—
She smiled with an expression that seemed to say, “Oh well, I guess I have no choice.”
“Looks like you get it. Well then, see you tomorrow morning. Let’s meet at the reception desk at 10:00.”
“Eh… Ah…”
“It’s 10 o’clock, right? At the hotel reception.”
“Y-yes. I und-understand……”
Even after changing clothes and getting into bed, I’m wide awake.
The reason I can’t seem to sleep at all isn’t so much because that incident was strange, but rather—
It’s because anger is simmering inside me.
(Hmm, come to think of it, that’s kind of weird, isn’t it…?)
(Even though I didn’t even ask for it!)
I was regretting— even now—that I had nodded along, swept up in the moment.
“S-Should I just skip this…!”
In the end……
I couldn’t stop thinking about Leon, and I couldn’t sleep until late at night.
And then, the next morning came……
I rub my sleepy eyes and sit up.
When I think back on yesterday, I still feel a bit unsettled —
(……I’d feel bad if I skipped this……)
After taking my time to get ready, I left the room with heavy steps.
When you take the elevator down to the ground floor, there you’ll find――
Just like yesterday, Leon—perfect down to every strand of hair—was waiting .
(W-Wow, you really came...)
As I stood there feeling strange, Leon’s gaze turned toward me.
He stepped up to right in front of me and asked briefly.
"Dinner?"
"...Not yet."
"Then let's have a meal first."
"Then, something light at the hotel restaurant—"
"Don't hold back. I was just wanting to eat out."
(Are you busy...!?)
He took me to a restaurant overlooking the sea.
I thought it was still early before opening, but perhaps we had arranged it beforehand...
The doors opened effortlessly, and the chef himself greeted us.
Maybe because of the hour, or perhaps they're clearing out the patrons.
There were no other patrons besides us.
"Vichyssoise and lamb roast."
After placing his order concisely, Leon turned his gaze toward me.
"Aria, what about you?"
"[主人公], what about you?"
"...Then, I'll have the same as Leon."
"Very well."
After the chef left the table.
The other waiters also disappeared, leaving us alone in this vast space.
"About the book you were holding yesterday."
Leon got straight to the point without any preamble.
"It's called an 'Original Text,' a very special kind of book."
"It is said that if you gather three of them, any wish will be granted."
It happened so suddenly that I couldn’t keep up with what was going on.
“There may be those who approach with malicious intent , trying to take it away.”
“So, I figured I needed to make time for you .”
I just can’t wrap my head around this—not even once, let alone twice or three times.
“So, what do you mean by ‘therefore’…?”
How does it all fit together?
Unable to fathom her intent, Leon furrowed his brow.

en: "Still not sure?"
“Oh, yes. I’m sorry.”
Leon let out a sigh of exasperation.
“So… Since there’s no other choice, from now on I’ll stick with you.”
“Wait, w-was that what it was all about…!?”
“Given the current flow, it’s pretty hard to pick up on that…!”
My true feelings slipped out before I knew it.
At that moment, Leon’s eyes widened for a split second.
“……Really? I’m sorry. I guess it was hard to understand.”
“I’m, I’m sorry… I’m just a little confused right now.”

"It's not as much of a long shot as you think."
"I can infer a lot from his position, and the odds are much better than in ordinary poker."

“……Leon is really amazing, isn’t he?”
“I wondered if this was someone who, despite being weak, loves gambling and ends up spending money recklessly…”
I accidentally let my true feelings slip.

“……So that’s how you felt……”
“S-Sorry…!”
“……Well, maybe I didn’t explain it well enough, but even so, there’s a lot of calculations going on behind the scenes, you know?”

“Your help was a big help. Thank you.”
Just give it to me, but…
Saying that with a smile, Leon looked more mature than usual.
Today is the day of my date with Finn.
Leon and I waited for dusk to fall, and I met up with him.
And then, following Finn’s guidance…
I visit the auction house where it’s said that items with a tainted history are put up for sale――
……The atmosphere here is different from the auction house the other day.
“Don’t stray too far from me. Unlike out here, not everyone here is a well-behaved customer.”
“Uh, yeah….”
At that moment.
I spotted someone I knew among the participants.

The digits are off.
As I stood there in shock, Leon whispered in my ear.

"I never imagined I'd meet you in a place like this. That's the Mirage for you."
…to think stolen goods are being auctioned.
This auction might be a rather shady affair.
"Next up, gold ornaments from ancient Orient—items that were displayed at the British Museum!"
"...That's a replica."
Speaking so that only we could hear, Evan murmured.
"Indeed, artifacts like that being stolen from the British Museum does happen quite often."

"So there's a back‑door deal, and the genuine piece has already been returned to the British Museum."

It seems Evan can see that person’s figure , though…
At my height, I’m hidden behind other people’s heads, and I can’t even tell where I am.
"Thirty-five million."
"Thirty-eight million!"
"……It's a one-on-one duel."
Finn watched them with an amused smile.
As the price kept rising, I grew anxious and tugged on Leon's sleeve.

en: “Leon… What did you just say?”
"It's a secret."
He said only that, then gave a small laugh.
Then, I stretch a little.
“I guess I had a little too much to drink yesterday… My head hurts, but maybe I’ll go get some breakfast.”
“I-Is that okay? You’re being so carefree…”
“Skipping meals isn’t good for your health. Even on a morning when you’re mistaken for a murderer.”
Even though it was a situation where he might get caught, Leon remains completely unfazed.
“B-but… Someone was killed, wasn’t they?”
“If the culprit isn’t found, Leon might end up getting arrested…”
“……I get it. If it bothers you that much, let’s find the real culprit. After breakfast, of course.”
“There’s no need to rush—there are still more than two weeks left until the festival ends.”
Saying that, Leon smiled.
He doesn’t look like someone who was so drunk last night.
(He’s putting on a front…!)
It doesn’t seem like they’re in any rush, though…
It’s also possible that they’re acting this way so I won’t have to worry.
(You might as well just speak your mind like you did yesterday ... you don’t have to hold back...)
It was quite a ordeal, but... I genuinely wanted to know what Leon really felt.
"By the way... you will help me find the culprit, of course, right?"
"Huh?"
He said it as if it were the most natural thing in the world, and I—
Of course I would...
Why would I?
"Well, of course I would..."
I hesitated, but I still agreed.
"I couldn't just stand by and do nothing after hearing a story like that..."
"You might be a little too kind... I worry you'll be taken advantage of so easily."
"I think you should work on that. You need to learn to be a bit more suspicious of people."
He spoke with a tone of exasperation, which I found quite hurtful.
……But I’m a little relieved by the candid, unreserved words .
"Since it’s Leon who’s being suspected, I don’t think I have any reason to join you in looking for the culprit ..."
Feeling a bit unsettled, I asked honestly.
Then...
Leon gave a daring smile.
It was a princely— —expression, vastly different from the face he wears when pretending to be a cat.
"You won’t understand unless you ask? Because you’re already tangled up in this."
A malicious edge seeped into his voice.
"After all, we spent the whole night together, didn’t we? And besides, you defended me earlier."
"If I'm the culprit, the Bureau will assume you know something about the circumstances."
"You might even be considered an accomplice. In other words――"
I realized my mistake, but it was already too late.
"If I don't escape this trouble, you'll be in a precarious position as well."
Had he forgotten to put on his mask?
His words were remarkably candid.
(Mr. Leon has been kind to me all this time, despite everything...)
Setting aside whether I'm involved or not, I can't bring myself to leave him behind.
"...Understood. I'll cooperate as well."
"Thank you. I knew you'd say that."
Mr. Leon smiled brightly.
...I should tell myself it's just my imagination that his smile feels a bit irritating.
When I came to the hotel restaurant for breakfast, I happened to run into Finn.
As we sat at the same table eating, he suddenly brought up the topic as if he’d just remembered.
“Come to think of it, it seemed kind of noisy this morning …”
“I wonder what happened? Do you know?”
“Um…”
“No, I don’t know anything about it. …Ariya feels the same way, right?”
“No, I don’t know anything about it. ……[主人公] probably feels the same way, right?”
“Finn. More importantly, regarding recent exchange rates, is there anything that concerns you?”
Leon subtly changes the subject.
Watching them talk about something rather complicated—
I think to myself absentmindedly.
(Putting the mystery aside for now… Leon, why are you looking out for me?)
I’ve been wondering about this from the very beginning.
(Just because we met when we were little, is that all it takes…?)
Judging by Leon’s behavior over the past few days, he doesn’t seem to be “kind to everyone.”
“I heard it’s a popular spot frequented by everyone from politicians to billionaires , so I was really looking forward to it.”
“It’s a shame the customer service is so poor.”
“Sorry, but I’m busy right now. I don’t have time to deal with you.”
“No. Please contact headquarters about that.”
The true intentions hidden behind rude behavior are often, surprisingly, just a kind gesture...
(Maybe you want the original book…?)
(Maybe you’ve collected three books and have a wish you want to make come true.)
However, Leon doesn’t seem to be actively trying to collect the original books.
Basically, if that’s the case, why didn’t you just tell me from the start that it was a book that grants wishes—
Just make up some excuse to talk your way out of it, then take the original book away.
“What’s wrong? You’ve gone quiet all of a sudden.”
He looks up at Finn’s words.

en: He didn’t call out to me—
It seems it was Leon’s side after all.
Looking somewhat melancholy, he gave a wry smile.
“Hmm… Actually, I think this muffin isn’t quite baked right.”
“Well then, should I share some of mine? I haven’t touched it yet, and it looks like it’s cooked just right.”
“No, it’s fine. You can eat that.”
Their back-and-forth is somehow endearing.
Despite the complex relationship between an adopted child and a biological child, I could tell they must get along well.
After finishing breakfast, where did Leon and I head next?
――It was at the office of Rudy, the Director of the Administration Bureau.
"Show me the investigation documents."
At Leon’s first words—uttered without the slightest hesitation— Rudy grimaced deeply.
“……Just when I thought you showed up out of the blue, what’s this? No matter what your position is, there’s no way I can forgive something like that――”
“The suspicion against me hasn’t been completely cleared, has it?”
He interrupts Rudy and continues.
“It’s unpleasant to have even the slightest room for doubt.”
“Le—Leon…!”
His choice of words was so blunt that I was the one who panicked.
“Above all, I know better than anyone else that I’m not the culprit.”
“So, I’ve decided to catch the real culprit myself and clear my name. Show me the investigation files.”
Faced with Leon’s reasoning—which, no matter how you look at it, was far too far-fetched— Rudy furrowed his brow in exasperation.
“The Administration must be busy, right? Once this case is resolved, there’ll be less extra work, which will be a relief for you guys too.”
Unable to bear watching Rudy’s as the furrow between his eyebrows deepened, I decided to speak up.
“Um, first of all, let me tell you in detail what we were doing yesterday …”
I went to the auction. I didn’t know it was illegal.
I headed home without winning any of the items at the auction, and went to a cabaret with Evan.
And then, we had another round of drinks in Leon’s room…
“Um, that guy Evan—it seems he wasn’t there when we went into the room ?”
“I think Evan must have woken up sometime in the early morning and returned to his room.”
Last night. The first one to get completely drunk was Evan.
It wouldn’t be strange if they woke up first.
“……Based on what you just said alone, I can’t say your innocence has been completely proven. ……Well, I get what you’re trying to say.”
As he said that, Rudy suddenly stood up from his chair.
“……I’m going to step away for just 10 minutes. There are investigation files on this desk. But make sure you don’t touch them under any circumstances.”
“! Rudy…”
“Before I get back, you guys need to get out of the room right away. Got it?”
Speaking in a tone of admonishment, he left the room.
“You’re surprisingly easy to get along with. It’s a relief that we can get straight to the point.”
Leon smiled, approached his desk, and immediately picked up the documents.
I joined him and peered into it as well.
The body appears to have been subjected to significant twisting throughout its entire length.
The muscle tissue and skeleton exhibit a spiral deformation, which visually closely resembles the state of a cloth-like object when tightly wrung out.
A nearly uniform degree of twisting is observed throughout the entire body, including the limbs and torso.
Based on the nature of this damage, it is highly likely that it resulted from an extremely strong external force or a similar impact .
Furthermore, based on the extent of the damage and the bleeding, after a comprehensive assessment, it is presumed that the injury in question was sustained while the victim was still alive.
Furthermore, no other injuries—such as cuts from a blade or bruises from a blunt object—were observed.
“The body was… twisted…?”
“……It’s hard to believe, but since that’s what it says, I guess that’s exactly how it was.”
“So the victim is the heir to the Sinclair conglomerate, is he?”
Included among the documents was what appeared to be a newspaper clipping . The photo showed a young man who looked familiar.
“! …I saw this person talking to Mei at the auction house.”
"Then, let's start by talking to her."
"Yes!"
By the time we left the Bureau, the sun was already setting.
"Um, Leon."
In the Director's office—based on his attitude toward Rudy, I asked about what had been on my mind.
"Today, you seemed a bit... different, Leon."
"It might just be my imagination, but you seemed less reserved than usual..."
Leon gave a wry smile, looking somewhat troubled.
"You're overthinking it. Besides, there's no need to be gentle with the people who've been suspecting me, is there?"
"More importantly, you're being suspected too, so you should be angrier about it."
"But from the Bureau's perspective, it's understandable that they find us suspicious..."
He let out a heavy sigh.
“……That side of you, really……”
“……I’m not so sure about that?”
(Even if you say that...)
I was at a loss for words.
It was on the way home that I suddenly felt something was off.
Suddenly, I could feel the tension in the air.
Just after I felt as if the scenery before my eyes had wavered for a moment……
“! Back then….”
Leon didn’t hesitate; he pulled out his gun.
On a quiet twilight street, deserted except for us, the sound of gunfire echoes.
It seemed like a hasty move, but...

“……So you really aren’t an ordinary human, are you?”

The young man steps forward casually.
Just then, overcome by a bad feeling, I instinctively took a step back.
Also, one step ahead of us is――

What happens if you touch “that” directly?
I freeze in terror as I imagine the outcome.
“Huh…?”

I instinctively glance around, but there’s no one there.
“A book, you say—”
The moment he muttered that.
That book appeared right before my eyes.
Someone is whispering in my ear.
Follow those instructions――
Before any doubts can arise, I reach for the book and pray from the bottom of my heart.
“Please protect us…!”
A strange “distortion” has drawn near—
I’m being blocked as if there were an invisible wall.
“! You… you didn’t actually read the original book, did you…?”
There’s a hint of tension in Leon’s voice.
Before he could finish speaking those words, he pulled the trigger again.
The young man who was hit by a bullet sways slightly.
Even so, I’ll try to take a step forward.
“……Don’t come here!”
I voiced my refusal.
Leon also pulled the trigger again—
The young man stopped moving.
……And then, a few seconds later.
Just as if swept away by the wind , it lost its shape.
“Huh…?”
What on earth happened?
I looked around in confusion, but there was no sign of that young man anywhere.
Just as I finally let out a sigh of relief—that’s when it happened.
My vision suddenly blurred, and I instinctively rubbed my eyes.
But after blinking a few times, my vision returned to normal.
Maybe I got some dust in my eye or something.
Right after I thought that.
“……That surprised me.”
I hear a familiar voice, and my shoulders jerk.
“So Jevshka got her hands on the original book, huh?”
When I looked over, there was――
There was Charles, smiling radiantly.
To ensure we wouldn’t be interrupted, Charles led us to a certain place.
That part...
It was a nighttime opera house enveloped in silence.
Maybe it’s a day off—there’s no sign of anyone around.
As if he were the master of this place, he walked with confidence, his footsteps echoing on the marble floor.
Then, she stops in her tracks and turns to look back at me gracefully.
“……Actually, I have the original book, too.”
Just as a dazzling light appeared in the space, the glow immediately converged toward his hand.
“...There. I hope this convinces you.”
A single book appeared.
The binding is different from the original book I own.
But, strangely enough, I got a similar impression.
“Meine Liebe. …I’ll get straight to the point: I’d like you to give me your book.”
“Huh…?”
“So—are you trying to say that the attack just now was your doing ?”
Even when met with a sharp retort, Charles’s expression remains unchanged.
“That wasn’t my doing.”
“Why? Because I didn’t know you owned the original book until just a moment ago.”
……Was that attack by that mysterious entity aimed at my original book?
(But even so...)
The first time you encounter “that thing.”
No one could have known that I actually owned the original book.
“If I continue to keep the original book as is, I’ll find myself in danger again.”
I'm not threatening you, but please consider it.
Charles smiled gently.
“Of course, I’m not asking you to just give it to me for free. If there’s anything I can do to make your wish come true, I’ll do it.”
I watch Leon closely.
He said nothing and stared at me as if leaving the decision up to me.
I am――
Why do you want the original book?
What do you mean, “anything”……
“Is there a reason why you want the original book, Mr. Charles?”
At least for me, I can’t immediately think of a wish I’d want to fulfill so badly that I’d go as far as hurting others to make it come true.
“……Princess’s question is valid, though……”
“We’re not close enough for me to tell you my personal wishes, are we?”
“……I suppose so.”
He’s right about that.
But...
“……I believe the power of this book could be misused if one were so inclined.”
“So, without knowing Mr. Charles’s purpose , I cannot hand it over.”
Suppose I let go of the book and am now safe.
This could potentially cause harm to others.
Thinking about it that way, I felt guilty about just letting it go so easily, and I hesitated.
“That’s true… You have a point.”
Charles nodded as if satisfied.
And then...
After hearing what I had to say, Leon was, for some reason, smiling contentedly.
“Leon?”
“No—I thought it hadn’t changed.”
“Huh?”
“……It’s nothing.”
“Anything… what do you mean?”
“That’s right—‘anything.’ Of course, there are limits to what I can do.”
“If that’s what you want, I’ll be your one-night lover—”
“……We’ve already got that covered.”
Mid-sentence, Leon interrupts with a sullen look on his face.
Leon turned to Charles once more and spoke.
“……On the other hand, is there any way I could get a copy of Charles’s book ?”
“If I could grant your wish—”
Without waiting for Leon to finish speaking, Charles shook his head slightly.
“That’s too bad, Monsieur Vitré.”
“No matter how much you may be the young president of Vitry Corporation , you just can’t do that.”
――This is not a wish that can be granted by money or power.
After implying this, Charles continued.
"…I’m not thinking of doing anything to you right now , but—"
"As long as either of us continues to hold the original manuscript , a clash will inevitably be unavoidable."
"When that time comes, I hope you won’t hold a strong grudge."
Charles smiled gently and turned his back on us.
After I watched him disappear into the back of the opera house, Leon opened his mouth.
There was a faint edge to his voice.
"You said the recent attack wasn’t your doing , but you can say whatever you want with your mouth."
"Be careful not to let your guard down too much around Charles ."
"…Yes."
I refused Charles’s request of my own accord.
By doing so, I realized that I had inadvertently thrown myself into the vortex of conflict over the original manuscript.
…Surely, the choice of whom to trust will determine my fate.
I had planned to visit her room today to speak with Mavis.
First, I had breakfast as usual.
As always, Leon was with me.
(If only I could have met her here, things would have been easier...)
I could not find Mavis in the restaurant.
"Good morning."
The one who spoke to me was Evan.
"Good morning, Evan."
"Yes. Thank you for the other day. It was an interesting night."
Lowering his voice, he continued.
"By the way, it seems one of the auction participants has died. I hear Mr. Vitry is being suspected?"
"Ah, that is..."
“I was questioned by the Administration Bureau, too. I told them everything I could remember, honestly.”
“……So we hit it off and had a few drinks, but we got a little too carried away and everyone ended up completely out of it, is that right?”
When Leon smiled at him, he smiled back and nodded.
“Right. I woke up at dawn, and still half-asleep, I went back to my room.”
“I wish I’d at least left a note behind.”
“Well, he said the crime took place around 11:00, so that makes it impossible for you guys.”
“Well… unless I use some kind of magic, that is.”
“I’ve already told the Administration Office that.”
“Thank you, Evan.”
“No. I just told the truth.”
After breakfast. Just as I was leaving the restaurant, Finn called out to me.
“Hey, you two. If you’ve got some time, why don’t we play a game of poker together?”
“In broad daylight…?”
“Apparently, if you ask the manager even in the morning, he’ll open the hall for you. What do you think?”
“Sorry, but I have something I need to do right now.”
When Leon flatly refused, Finn shrugged his shoulders in disappointment.
“I see… Well, I guess there’s no helping it. Let’s hang out again sometime.”
After Finn left—
Leon looks at me and says, as if urging me on.
“Well then, let’s go see her. I hope she’s still in her room.”
“Huh? But….”
“! I’m staying at Azur, too. We might run into each other again.”
“I heard you were staying here, but I didn’t know your room number…”
“Ah. Well, it’ll work out somehow.”
Leon nodded nonchalantly and walked over to the receptionist.
As I watched to see what he was planning to do...
“Hey, can I talk to you for a sec?”
“Yes. How may I help you?”
“Sorry to bother you when you’re busy… The Administration asked me to do something.”
Leon smiled warmly.
(……There’s a cat on my head……)
Leon boldly used the name “Administration Bureau” as a shield, but—
I haven’t been officially asked to investigate this, so naturally, I have no authority whatsoever.
His words weren’t exactly lies, but they certainly weren’t the whole truth.
“I can’t go into details, but I’m here on business with one of the guests.”
“Could you tell me where a woman named Mavis’s room is?”
“……T-that’s……”
“Well, if it’s too much trouble, it’s fine if you turn me down …”
He whispers to the conflicted employee.
“The Administration seems to be getting impatient. It looks like they want the information as soon as possible.”
If you cooperate, they'll probably be happy too, right?
"Even if something happens, I'll take responsibility I want you to feel at ease... How does that sound?"
He gently initiates the negotiation.
As a result, it didn't take long for the hotel staff to give in.
With just a few words we coaxed out the guest room info, and got off the lift on the floor where Ms. Mei is staying.
We knocked on the door several times, but there was no response.
Could they be away?
Just when I thought it might be better to come back later—
"—Ughyaa!"
A shout from inside the room could be heard.
"Eh—"
Leon immediately grabbed the door handle.
Perhaps the door wasn't locked, it opened smoothly—
Following Leon, I rush into the room.
There, I see Mavis shielding someone who has collapsed behind her.
The person she is facing is the young man who spoke to Leon before.
