en: The blond young man—William—does not look our way, his gaze fixed downward on Mavis.
—She is about to be attacked.
That was my immediate intuition.
(I have to protect her...!)
Instinctively, I plead with the original text.
The chair, the desk, the furniture in the room lift into the air—and—
Suddenly, with a force strong enough to sweep the young man away, they rain down like bullets.
Blown back, the young man drops to one knee, glaring at us.
“Don’t move!”
Leon, gun in hand, shouts for them to stop.
But Mr. William didn’t hesitate; he turned his back on me—
He dove through the window, protecting only his head.
This is the <dic=501> second floor </dic>.
"To just leap out like that without hesitation," I gasped.
……At that moment.
Everything went black before my eyes.
“Huh…?”
Almost the moment he blinked in confusion, a sharp pain shot through the back of his eye.
Holding my eyes shut in the darkness, I endured the confusion , and before long—
Light returned to my vision.
(What was that just now…?)
An indescribable chill crept down my spine.
“Percy……”
I hear Mei’s weak voice and snap back to reality.
As she looked, she saw that she was gripping Mr. Percy’s collar tightly as he lay on the ground.
I rush toward the two of them as if propelled forward.
“Ah—”
The moment I saw that, my mind couldn’t keep up.
Even though I know it’s him, I can’t recognize him with my eyes.
Percy’s body is strangely… all over the place—
It was distorted.
That’s the only way to describe it. As a human being, it has a shape that shouldn’t exist.
……So, just by glancing at that scene, I knew he was dead.
“……Well, he’s my friend, after all. I listen to what he says a lot, so don’t worry too much about it.”
“I’ll handle the technical side. Using the spell formula we’ve constructed, we’ll form ‘him’…”
“You use the magic of the original book to ensure its manifestation. This is a wonderfully well-matched arrangement. …Don’t you think so?”
After that...
Before long, the Administration Bureau arrived on the scene.
We, who were present, were asked to accompany them to Portail Bleu...
I ended up having to explain the entire sequence of events, step by step, to Rudy.
After we finished talking.
……Next, what Mei began to say was something unexpected.
“Two people walked into the room. One was that blond man, and the other was—”
“A man wearing a black robe. His face was hard to make out; he looked like he could be either a child or an adult…”
(! Wait a minute...)
I exchanged glances with Leon and nodded.
“The man in the robe tried to do ‘something’ to me. …That’s the only way I can put it.”
"He wasn't holding a weapon or anything, but... I felt he was dangerous."
"And then..."
Ms. Mavis, her face pale, spoke without changing her expression.
"Percy stepped in... and shielded me."
"By the time I realized what was happening, he was already like that. ...In an instant."
"I tried to support the fallen Percy, and... in the moment I looked away, the man in the robe was already gone."
"Only the blond man was left in the room. And there, they were."
After Ms. Mavis finished explaining the entire incident, Mr. Ulysse spoke up.
"...The body left at the scene was, so to speak, twisted all over by an extremely powerful force."
"It closely resembles the state of the victim's body from the incident involving the Sinclair conglomerate's Hope Diamond auction."
"...There is no proof, but judging by the circumstances alone, it is highly likely to be the same perpetrator."
No one answered Mr. Leon's murmur.
That is not a denial—
If anything, it was a silence that implied agreement.
“……It was Mavis Redmond, wasn’t it? Do you have any idea why she was targeted?”
“……I don’t think I’ve lived my life in a way that would make people resent me. If there is a reason, it might be because of my status.”
She let out a small breath and said quietly.
“I am Lady Rosemary. …The daughter of the Duke of Sutherland.”
“S-Sutherland… you mean that paramedic!?”
Formed primarily around upper-class women, such as the nobility of the United Kingdom――
An emergency medical team that serves as nurses in the military and continues to treat people at hospitals in the Republic and elsewhere.
……The wife of a certain duke, as well as his daughter, are also participating as rescue team members.
It’s a famous story that often appears in the newspapers.
“……Does the Duke’s family have any political rivals?”
“Just because I’m part of the emergency response team, I never would’ve thought my life would be threatened like this.”
“Please hear me out until the end.”
Faced with the question, Mei gave a wry smile.
“As the duke’s daughter, I came to Mirage to take on the role of <dic=308> Sherpa </dic>.”
“……Well, there are actually a few other errands I’ve been tasked with . But I’ll take care of those while I’m at it.”
“Sherpa…?”
“……I see.”
Their expressions showed that they were convinced.
It seems I was the only one who didn’t quite understand the meaning of that phrase.
Perhaps noticing my confusion, Leon steps in to provide further explanation.
“A Sherpa is a person who carries out ‘coordination’ on behalf of the extremely busy heads of state from various countries.”
“I’m not exactly making a big deal out of it, but it’s been this way for a long time.”
“To maintain global balance, nations are secretly holding <dic=113> the Council of Sages </dic>.”
“The agenda varies from time to time, but it’s things like avoiding a war that might break out in the future…”
“Or perhaps its purpose is to negotiate a peace treaty for a war that has already broken out.”
“……Um, how do you know about that secret existence, Leon?”
Even as they listened to the explanation, Rudy and the others didn’t seem surprised.
Seeing my confusion, Leon was the first to respond.
“Of course—I’m a Sherpa, too.”
……A memory surfaced in my mind, making me wonder, “Could it be…?”
“If you’re not willing to cooperate, that’s fine with me… But as long as you’re staying on this island, you do know what kind of treatment you’ll receive, don’t you?”
"I'm here as a Sherpa."
(……So that’s how it was……)
Leon revealed his “identity.”
And then, having learned of the existence of the Sherpa , I wondered if Rudy had backed down—
Finally, it all made sense to me.
“Naturally, the intentions of the leaders of each country vary. After all, every country prioritizes its own interests above all else.”
"Even if only the busy ones had to discuss until they reached mutual agreement, that's not realistic, is it?"
“That’s why ‘someone’ acts as the country’s spokesperson to proceed with negotiations in advance.”
“That is how the Sherpa system works, and that is the role of the Council of Sages.”
……Hearing that reminded me of a certain conversation.
“There are even rumors that influential figures from various countries are gathering in Mirage to hold a conference that will determine the course of world affairs— .”
I realize now that it wasn’t just a rumor after all.
“……Did Rudy and the others also know about the Sherpas’ existence ?”
“To some extent, yes. Mirage is often chosen as a venue for meetings .”
“I-Is that so…!?”
“A politically neutral place where external interference is difficult. …It’s ideal for negotiations between nations.”
“External interference is difficult”—
“So… does that mean the Sherpa meeting will continue during the festival?”
“Ah. A meeting that will determine the future of the country —there’s no way it would end in just a day or two, is there?”
Leon agreed without hesitation.
Next, Mei calmly adds some additional information.
“After all, it’s not like the island’s administration and the Sherpas are working together, is it?”
“Only we, the parties involved, can announce the meeting.”
“Even if the Administration were to become aware of this, they must strictly maintain a policy of non-interference.”
I thought it was just a beautiful island, but on this Mirage...
To be honest, I never even considered that there might be schemes unfolding that would involve the entire world.
“Still, I never would have thought the Duke’s daughter would be this Sherpa. The United Kingdom really took a bold step.”
“I just said I want to do what I like.”
“Then, as a condition, I was forced to take on the role that everyone else had been avoiding.”
Mei gave a small, wry smile.
Then, he looks at me and adds a few words.
“The Vitoris have served as Sherpas for generations. I hear they’re called up almost every time.”
“It seems there was a period when the finances were in trouble and it was taken down for a few years . But it looks like things have picked up again recently, right?”
“……Even though I didn’t tell you to keep it a secret, isn’t it a bit questionable to reveal another company’s financial situation without asking for permission?”
Leon looks at her with a dissatisfied expression.

en: But Mei acts as if she knows nothing about it.
“It’s common knowledge, isn’t it? I don’t feel the need to keep something like this—which would make the newspapers —a secret.”
“……Is that so?”
When I timidly asked, Leon let out a sigh.
“……It’s true. In recent years, the Vitry family’s business has been struggling, and until about five years ago, they were on the verge of ruin.”
“Ever since my father stepped down as president, we’ve somehow managed to turn things around.”
“……Thanks to the new military supply division you created.”
Vitry was, indeed, a world-renowned billionaire.
I didn’t know the business was on the brink of collapse, though…
Everyone knows that in recent years, the company has expanded into the arms industry and is reaping enormous profits.
“A few people are selected from each country to be Sherpas based on factors such as family background or occupation.”
“No matter the era, if you’re a merchant of death, you’re highly likely to be appointed as a Sherpa.”
“Where to distribute the latest weapons, and how many? Which countries to sell them to, and at what price…?”
“With that choice, couldn’t you influence the course of the battle however you want?”
“It’s like moving pieces on a chessboard—that’s how you’ve been manipulating the balance of the world, right?”
“……I won’t deny it, though.”
He responded with a consistently gentle demeanor.
“……Something like that…….”
I find the very existence of Sherpas terrifying.
I also feel a sense of revulsion at the fact that so many lives have been determined with the same casual ease as if it were just a game.
But...
“Don’t be so scared, okay? We’re not exactly an evil organization or anything.”
Mei gave a wry smile.
“Without someone to control the world, neither war nor economic panic will be kept in check.”
“Sherpa is the system designed to prevent such ‘worst-case scenarios,’ .”
“Well, there might be some people who attend meetings just to line their own pockets .”
Mei casts a meaningful glance at Leon.
Then, Leon smiled and shrugged his shoulders.
“I’m not working as a Sherpa for the money or for power.”
“I don’t intend to prolong the war to make a profit, nor do I have any grand ambitions like striving for world peace, or anything of that sort.”
“For me, as long as I had the status and financial means to come to this island, that was enough.”
“To come to this island, you say…”
Interrupting Mei, who was about to speak, Leon forcefully changes the subject.
“Let’s get down to business.”
“The agenda for this Council of Sages is to find a resolution to the world war that has already been raging for nearly three years.”
“If the peace talks cannot proceed as scheduled, naturally, the war will drag on.”
“Ah… Well then, this attack might be the work of someone who doesn’t want to stop the war.”
“If the Sherpa dies, the meeting cannot continue. Even if he’s alive, just being suspected will leave him unable to move.”
“Was the winning bidder for the Hope Diamond killed because of that…?”
“It’s not entirely impossible, I suppose.”
“Still, the meeting won’t be canceled just because one or two people are missing , and while I do think it’s a rather roundabout way of doing things…”
“For example, if Leon Vitry were to die , the whole island would be in an uproar, wouldn’t it?”
“It’s a whole different story from me, who’s here undercover. That’s probably why they framed me for a crime I didn’t commit.”
I didn’t want to cause a fuss—
That’s certainly a possibility.
“Um… Suppose that disrupting the Council of Sages was the culprit’s objective…”
“Why do you want to prolong the war?”
So many people have lost their lives, and yet the country just keeps getting poorer.
“Is there really anyone who hopes the war will never end…?”
Mei lowered her eyes slightly.
“……It’s a shame, but there are so many of them.”
Leon quietly continued speaking.
"War is a money game."
"The victorious nations gain money, production capacity, and land. The defeated nations are burdened with reparations and lose out."
He said it outright, without a hint of remorse.
"Because demand is clear, doing business is easier."
"It's not just weapons dealers like me. Ironworks and even shipbuilding are also quite profitable."
"The value of food and medical supplies also skyrockets."
"…While the common folk are forced into a harsh life, there aren't few people raking in enormous profits."
I thought I knew that the world isn't built solely on noble ideals.
Nevertheless…
Sacrificing people for money—
I felt a considerable resentment toward those who desire war for their own profit.
――After finishing the interrogation and the discussion about the Sherpas, we left the director's office.
Walking down the quiet, empty hallway, Mavis spoke up.
"……Aria. May I ask you something?"
"……[主人公]. May I ask you something?"
Mavis stopped me with a serious expression.
"When you all rushed into my room, you were holding a strange book."
"! That was……."
Should I answer?
Leon spoke up on my behalf, as I hesitated.
"You've probably heard the stories, right? That is the original manuscript."
"……Well, it's a fairly famous rumor, but I never thought it actually existed."
"You wanted to come to Le Mirage, for that original manuscript?"
Leon did not answer that question.
“Please keep it a secret that Aria has the original book.”
“Please keep it a secret that she has the original book.”
“If this becomes known, her position will be in jeopardy.”
Mei looked at Leon and me in that order and nodded.
“I won’t reveal any information about the person who saved my life. I promise.”
Leon and I said goodbye to Mei and left the Administration Bureau.
It’s far too dangerous for her, having just been targeted, to return to the hotel without an escort.
Going forward, it seems Mei will be placed under the protection of the Administration Bureau until the situation settles down.
The two of them walk side by side through the peaceful streets.
Meanwhile, he—
……Is he lost in thought or something?
He remained silent for a long time, which was unlike him.
“Leon?”
Even when I try to talk to them, there’s no response.
(Come to think of it, this happened before too...)
“What’s wrong? You’ve gone quiet all of a sudden.”
“Leon! Are you thinking about something…?”
“! Ah, uh... Um, sorry. What were we talking about?”
He smiled as if to cover it up.
To be honest, I’m worried about whether this will work.
“……Um, are you getting enough rest at night? You look tired.”
It’s no wonder he’s exhausted after being falsely accused.
Even if they seem to be acting normally on the surface, they might actually be mentally exhausted.
“That’s nothing you need to worry about.”
I was abruptly and rudely cut off.
It’s hard to believe this is the same person who was just talking so politely with Mei and the others.
Seeing my surprise, Leon looked away, seeming a little awkward.
“……Ah, no. ……I’m getting enough sleep. Sorry for sounding so sharp.”
“As for work, there aren’t many options on this island, so I’m sleeping more than twice as much as usual.”
“Well, once the meeting starts, things will get busy, so I need to make sure I’m well-rested.”
“More importantly……――”
He fixes me with a serious gaze.
“Aria. Please give me your original book.”
“[主人公]. Give me your original book.”
“Eh—”
The words, which seemed almost forceful, took my breath away.
But his gaze remains unwavering.
“……You remember what Evan said, right? That magic comes at a price.”
"Ah, yes..."
“Magic is inherently dangerous, and using it requires a price to pay….”
……Come to think of it, I do remember us talking about something like that.
“You were worried about your eyes after using the original book, weren’t you?”
(! …I had noticed that.)
I suddenly remember that my vision went completely dark and a pain began deep within my eyes.
“……I thought… maybe that was due to the price I paid .”
“Someone who can’t use magic uses the grimoire to cast spells. I wonder if that might result in a greater backlash than usual.”
“……Watching you, it occurred to me.”
A magical book that grants any wish.
In a sense, it may be only natural that this involves some risk.
“I never asked you outright, but… You don’t actually want the original book, do you?”
“I knew it. He didn’t even make a move to collect the other books .”
Leon wasn’t trying to collect them either.
But...
Judging from what he’s said so far, unlike me, he has a compelling reason to seek out the original book.
(Earlier, Leon said he came to the island for the original book ...)
I ask hesitantly.
“……Leon, you want the original book, don’t you?”
“Why didn’t you try to take the original book away from me ?”
“It’s a given. That’s because you’re the one who obtained it.”
He answers calmly.
“I thought that owning the original book might actually work in your favor .”
“But….”
Leon furrows his brow slightly.
“If it becomes known that you possess it, it’s inevitable that you’ll be targeted by others.”
“Furthermore, if used to protect yourself, a cost will be incurred.”
“I didn’t think it was a good idea to let you keep something so dangerous.”
“It’s not like I asked for this, after all. Besides, I’m always using it for other people…”
“N-No, that’s not true.”
It was to protect myself— and because I wanted to protect Mei, I used it.
I definitely didn’t use it just for other people.
But Leon shook his head.
“From my perspective, you should act more selfishly .”
“You, too, must have one or two wishes you’d like to see come true, right?”
Both when Charles asked me to give him the original book and now, I’ve asked myself the same question.
But I still don’t feel like this is something I need.
“……I’m already able to enjoy happiness that’s within my means .”
“I was able to come to the island I’d always dreamed of, and even after my father passed away, thanks to the help of those around me, I’ve managed to survive until now.”
"…There are no wishes I'd like the original book to grant  none."
Upon hearing that reply, Leon—
For some reason, he frowned in a petulant way.
"Aria. You should be more selfish."
"[主人公] should be more selfish."
"There are as many fun things,  happy things as there are stars in the world, you know?"
"Desire more and stretch out your hand.  Don't be satisfied with a life that limited."
"Eh, wh‑what...!?"
Why am I being scolded?
Suddenly, those words from that night echo in my mind.
"Why don't you become more selfish?"
"Say you want what you want! Then,  I'll properly…"
...I don't quite understand, but he's serious.
Irritation and a hint of anxiety seep into his expression.
I felt no reason to doubt that those words came from his true heart.
"...Then, um."
"What is the wish you want to see come true, Leon...?"
He falls silent for a moment.
Then, lowering his gaze, he smiles as if—
reminiscing about something.
"...My wish isn't anything grand. At least, that's what others would say."
"It's a trivial wish from when I was a child."
"It's been decided for a long time. I've lived my life up to now solely for that purpose."
Though he didn't reveal the details.
Those words seemed to hold no falsehood.

“That’s right. …Keeping the original book is a matter of life and death for you.”
“I might get attacked like today, and to protect myself, I might end up hurting the other person.”
Rudy fixed his gaze on me and asked briefly.
“……Are you prepared for that?”
“If you tell me something like that out of the blue…”
I’ve only just learned about magic and the book known as the “Original Text” for the very first time.
Even when asked if I was prepared for that, I couldn’t answer.
“You don’t know anything. Even just a moment ago, you would have been killed if I hadn’t been there.”
He narrowed his eyes and spoke in a dismissive tone.
“Ownership of the original book is lost when you indicate your intention to transfer it, or—when you die.”
“Death……”
At those words, a chill ran down my spine.
“So, give that to me.”
“Huh…?”
“The Administration Bureau is responsible for managing the recovered original books.”
The Administration Bureau is the organization responsible for maintaining public order on the island.
It seems only natural that they would try to control the source text, which could become a source of conflict.
But...
“If I hand this over, won’t Rudy and the others be targeted next—”
He cut me off and said coldly.
“I’m different from you. I can use magic, and even if I’m attacked, I can fight back.”
“Besides, if I had the power of the original book, I wouldn’t let the attackers get away like I did just now.”
Even so, as I was mulling over whether it was really okay to just hand this over so easily...
“……You still can’t figure out something this simple?”
“For someone like you who doesn’t even know anything about magic, it’s useless anyway. Just get rid of it already.”
The voice, speaking matter-of-factly and curtly, seemed to be berating me.
Is he really requesting the original text solely for the sake of maintaining public order?
Since I don’t know the person, I can’t judge right away.
“……Do you have a wish you’d like to make come true, Mr. Rudy ?”
He seemed to stumble over his words for just a moment.
But she immediately opens her mouth with an annoyed expression.
“My wish is for there to be no unnecessary conflict on this island. I want to bring this festival to a safe conclusion. …That’s all.”
“……There’s no way I’d use something like this for my own selfish gain.”
Are those words spoken with sincerity?
Or is there another underlying reason?
Still unsure, I say.
“Well then… could you tell me a little about yourself?”
Didn’t you see that coming? Rudy’s eyes widened in surprise.
“I don’t really know much about Rudy, whom I just met yesterday.”
“Of course, I’m grateful for your help earlier. …But if….”
I continue speaking cautiously.
“Well, if Rudy were to get his hands on the original book and intended to misuse it…”
“Wha…! There’s no way I’d do something like that…!”
“W-well, that might be true, but with words you can say just about anything…!”
Rudy clamped his mouth shut, looking annoyed.
“W-Well, if I give the original book to Rudy, it might cause trouble for a lot of people.”
“So, once I get to know you and feel I can really trust you…”
“I’ll leave the original book with you. …Well then, is that not okay?”
Rudy was staring at me intently with a sharp gaze, but...
Eventually, his expression softened slightly.
“……I get it. Fine. You do have a point.”
“Oh, thank you so much…!”
“……So you really are that person’s grandchild, aren’t you? I finally feel like I’ve come to realize it, just a little bit.”
I wonder if Grandma and I are somehow alike in some way.
“Besides, your offer comes at just the right time. I was planning to protect you anyway.”
“Protection…?”
When I tilt my head, he continues the conversation as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
“You told someone, didn’t you? That you got your hands on the original book.”
“No, I didn’t say that. I found out I had that book when I was attacked…”
“Huh?”
“Could it be that… using some kind of magic… someone found out that I’m the owner of this book…?”
“No, that’s not…”
Rudy murmurs in a voice tinged with confusion.
But perhaps he quickly regained his composure. He continued with a calm expression.
"… The reason is aside, since you are actually being attacked, that man knew that you have the original manuscript."
“There’s no guarantee that someone didn’t see what happened earlier, so I can’t leave you alone.”
“……I mean, it’s a miracle we made it out alive. I guess our opponent let their guard down, too.”
“It looks like there are allies over there, so you’d better assume there won’t be a second chance.”
As that man walks away.
I ask him, recalling how Rudy had been keeping a watchful eye on his surroundings.
“Was there anyone else there…?”
“……When that man fled, it was as if he were hiding himself —darkness fell, didn’t it?”
“He didn’t seem to have the strength to do that himself. Someone must have let him escape.”
“Then why didn’t the two of them attack me together…?”
“Well… You had something in mind, didn’t you? Like, you were planning to focus solely on withdrawal support, or something.”
Upon hearing that, he began to wrap up the conversation.
“Anyway, we’re going to keep you safe. You’ll be staying at the Administration Bureau for a while.”
“Staying at a hotel alone is dangerous, and it could involve other guests.”
They say it’s “protection,” but that probably means it will be placed under the Administration Bureau’s surveillance.
To be honest, I’m a bit reluctant.
“In that case, wouldn’t this house work? I’m alone, and it’s closer to the Administration Bureau than the hotel.”
Rudy shakes his head without a moment’s hesitation.
“No way. I can’t protect you when it really counts, and we don’t have enough personnel to constantly send someone out.”
“……I understand.”
I accepted this and nodded reluctantly.
“……And don’t even think about using the original book just out of curiosity. Magic is a terrifying thing.”
“An ordinary person who isn’t even a mage—without the knowledge or resolve— shouldn’t be handling this.”
Even though I was completely absorbed in the attack, I used the power of the original book to hurt someone.
That fact remains unchanged.
I felt as though he had seen right through the fear I’d been harboring deep in my heart regarding the original text.
"Feel free to use this room."
After talking at Grandma’s house, I was taken by Mr. Rudy to the Administration Office.
The room I was led to was small but surprisingly cute.
“I’ll have someone pick up the luggage at the hotel later. Let me know if there’s anything else you need.”
“It’s fine to walk around inside Portail Bleu. I think staying in your room all the time would be suffocating.”
“……But even here, you must absolutely never tell anyone that you have the original book.”
“Even the agency staff, too?”
“Yeah. I don’t plan on telling you for now. You never know where information might leak from.”
"I understand... Thank you."
After conveying what needed to be done, Rudy turned his back on me and walked out of the room.
“……Phew.”
I found myself alone in the room and unconsciously exhaled.
(This has turned into quite a mess...)
Just as I was thinking that.
“? Yes?”
I hear a knock on the door and respond instinctively.
Just as I was wondering if I’d forgotten to mention something —
“Good morning, Aria….”
“Good morning, [主人公]…….”
“Ahès!”
Were you sleeping just a moment ago? She rubs her eyes sleepily.
“I’m… so glad you came… Let’s play… a lot…”
“Did you hear about me from someone?”
Wondering why the visitor had arrived so early, I asked, and Ahès pointed at the door.
“I just ran into Rudy over there a moment ago…”
“I see… Come to think of it, Ahès lives here, doesn’t she?”
“I’ll be staying here for a while, too. I’d be happy if we could get along.”
When I smiled, she smiled back contentedly.
“Hehe… We’re already best friends, aren’t we…?”
The next morning...
Maybe I was tired from everything that happened yesterday, but it seems I slept soundly.
When I looked at the clock in the room, it was already past 10 o’clock.
(I overslept…!)
I hurriedly climbed out of bed and, by the time I’d finished getting myself ready for the moment,
“――Yes, yes!”
Hearing the sound of a knock on the door, I hurriedly answer.
“Good morning. From the hotel room I brought your luggage over.”
The visitor was Ms. Yuris, the Deputy Director, whom I had met before.
“Thank you, Yuris.”
“No, no. It looks like you got a good night’s sleep last night, didn’t you?”
“Huh? Oh, yes.”
“Rudy told me yesterday, and I went to pick it up right away, but I haven’t heard back from him at all.”
“Ah…! I’m sorry…!”
It seems he visited my room even while I was asleep.
Yuris didn’t change her expression in the slightest and continued in a friendly manner.
"Well, if there’s anything you don’t understand or if you run into any trouble, feel free to ask me or any other staff member."
“I understand. It’s helpful to hear you say that.”
“You’re free to do as you please, but please don’t enter the lab or other areas without permission .”
"If you’re unsure whether it’s okay to enter a certain area, please ask a nearby station attendant or child."
“Also, it seems you’ll need Rudy’s permission to leave the Administration Bureau?”
With a wry smile, Yuris said that, then lowered her voice to ask.
“……So, what on earth did you do to end up here?”
“Ah… That’s…”
To explain that, I have to talk about the original book.
“Would it be okay if I asked Rudy about this? …I’m not sure if I should bring it up.”
“Hmm…”
“……Well then, let’s have breakfast for now. I’ll show you to the lounge.”
When I entered the room that Yuris had shown me to, Rudy was already seated there.
Meals are set out at his seat and the seat across from him.
“Wow, that looks delicious. I’m surprised— You’ve been making something so elaborate first thing in the morning?”
After reacting in a somewhat over-the-top manner, he smiled at Rudy.
“Well, I’m going back to work. Rudy will take care of the rest.”
After saying just that, he hurriedly walked away.
“Good morning…….”
“……Good morning.”
“Mr. Rudy, you’re so busy, yet I’ve caused you trouble… I’m sorry.”
Yesterday, I didn’t have the time to apologize properly.
When I told him that again, he looked away for a moment.
“……It’s fine, don’t worry about it. Since I said I’d protect you, I’ll take responsibility.”
“! Thank you very much.”
I thought he was a strict and serious person, but…
It might actually be surprisingly well-maintained.
“……Um. Is it okay if I sit down?”
When I asked hesitantly, he nodded silently.
Sitting across from Rudy, I let my gaze drift toward the delicious-looking dish.
A salad topped with fresh vegetables and a little fruit.
The quiche with salt-cured pork and spinach looks nicely browned and delicious.
The onion potage, with melted cheese stirred in, is also giving off a wonderful aroma.
“The chef at Portail Bleu is amazing…! Everything looks delicious!”
“……It’s me.”
“I made breakfast today.”
“……What?!”
“Why are you so surprised? Aren’t you overreacting?”
“I’m sorry! Well, that’s a bit unexpected…”
I apologize in a panic.
Rudy didn’t scold me; he just said...
“……I’m not sure if it’s to your taste, but please help yourself.”
“Y-yes. I’ll have some…!”
I immediately cut a slice of quiche and took a bite.
The gentle sweetness of the egg, the saltiness of the pork, and the bitter aftertaste of the spinach combine to create—
This is the best quiche I’ve ever had.
“……Wow! Rudy, you could be a chef!”
“……That won’t happen. I’m the director, after all.”
Rudy briefly denied, but it also looks like he's raising his mouth corners proudly.
“I cook too, but I’m just average—or rather, I’m not very good at it…”
“I couldn’t make something this elaborate. Especially starting first thing in the morning!”
I can see why Yuris was so surprised.
“……Cooking and magic have some things in common, you know.”
“First, the theory—<dic=904> recipe </dic>. If you follow the set procedure correctly, you’ll end up with something delicious.”
“Cooking depends on the ingredients, but magic, on the other hand, requires you to control and adjust yourself.”
“One thing we can all agree on is… That both are quite deep, I suppose.”
As he says this, he seems happier than ever.
“So, you really like Rudy, don’t you?”
Magic is
Cooking is
“About magic.”
Rudy fell silent at my words.
Then, with a stern expression, he replied matter-of-factly.
“……It’s not about liking or disliking, or anything like that.”
“Oh… Sorry, that was a weird thing to say.”
I feel awkward, wondering if I went too far with what I said.
“You seem to really love cooking.”
“Not really, that’s not true.”
Rudy replied briefly, saying only that.
(I wonder if that’s right…?)
It definitely looked like he liked it, though...
It would be strange for me to contradict what he said himself, so I’ll refrain from pressing the issue.
Just as we finished eating, Rudy began talking about today’s plans.
“I have to go on my daily patrol. Would you mind coming with me?”
Patrol――
I realized that was why I’d seen him all over the island yesterday.
“It’s only been a day since yesterday, so security at Portail Bleu hasn’t been reinforced yet.”
“It’s safer for you to stay by my side than to stay here.”
“……Understood. I’ll do my best.”
Remembering that I had been attacked last night , I nodded back, feeling a little nervous.
Shortly after starting the patrol.
“Hey, Director.”
A woman on the island calls out to Rudy.
“This year, so many guests are coming all the way to Vil It’s noisy even at night. Can’t we do something about this?”
Starting with that complaint, many people began approaching Rudy.
“You did make sure to turn away any strange visitors, right? Please be careful to choose who you let onto the island.”
“Ah, Rudy. It’s about my cow, but he hasn’t been eating much lately….”

en: Topics range from island security to neighborhood disputes, and even extend to meals and yard work.
“The Administration will handle the nighttime disturbances appropriately. In fact, staff members have been patrolling since yesterday.”
“We conducted the island entry screening using the same standards as every year, so don’t worry.”

en: “……Rudy Rochefort. Director of the Mirage Administration Bureau.”
“So, what are you doing here? on the blackboard. Was there a word you didn’t understand?”
When asked, Jack slumped his shoulders.
“Ah… I get the meaning, but I don’t understand the content.”
“What do you mean…?”
“For example, this Niçoise salad. How is it different from the Normandy-style one?”
“Gratin Dauphinois is ‘a gratin from the Dauphiné region,’ right? …So, what kind of dish is it?”
Now that you mention it, you’re right.
“Unless you’re familiar with the Republic’s local cuisine, you wouldn’t know right away, would you…?”
“The cuisine of the United Kingdom is more straightforward. It’s easy to imagine what’s inside just from the name.”
“For example, fish and chips, right? <dic=307> Shepherd’s pie </dic>, roast beef……”
“Even in the United Kingdom, there are dishes named after places, right? Like Yorkshire pudding.”
After correcting Jack’s words, Rudy begins to explain matter-of-factly.
“The Niçoise style often uses tomatoes, hard-boiled eggs, black olives, and salted fish.”
“Normandy-style cuisine features cidre, or apples themselves. It includes plenty of shellfish and crustaceans.”
“……Well, if you’re not sure, just ask a staff member, or order today’s special.”
“The cuisine of the Republic—especially Mirage’s— is always delicious; you can’t go wrong with anything.”
After hearing his explanation, Jack nodded thoughtfully, Hmm.
“So, the only remaining issue is the budget, then.”
Sitting on a chair at the café, Rudy says as if taking a deep breath.
“There are plenty of delicious things on this island at reasonable prices, after all.”
“Ah, ah…”
Before he knew it, he found himself sitting there with them. Jack nodded, feeling a bit overwhelmed.
Today’s recommendation is surprisingly expensive.
As for how expensive it is, it’s enough to buy about 20 baguettes in Paris.
(Serge pays for my meals, but...)
I do want to keep it as modest as possible.
While Jack and I were looking at the menu and deep in thought—
“Mussels steamed in white wine. White fish fritters. Lobster gratin. And then….”
“Onion tart and carrot soup. Divide it into three portions and bring them over.”
Rudy quickly finished placing his order.
“If we split it among everyone, we can eat all kinds of things more cheaply, right? …Is there a problem?”
“Oh, no, that’s a relief.”
“I’m happy too. I want to eat a lot…!”
I can’t quite hide how excited I am.
Comparing myself to Mr. Rudy, who still had a serious look on his face—
Jack chuckled softly.
Fortunately, the café was empty today, and my food arrived without much of a wait.
“! It’s delicious……!”
“What is this…? It’s just steamed clams, right? So why does it taste like this…?”
“The shallots have a nice texture, don’t they? I also deliberately chose a white wine with strong acidity.”
“……What’s going on with the Republic’s cuisine? This gratin over here has an incredibly rich flavor, too….”
“Around here—the Iroise Sea is a great spot for catching lobster, isn’t it?”
When I looked at Rudy as if seeking his approval, he nodded vigorously.
“That’s why you can eat here for less than in Paris. Plus, it’s fresh and delicious.”
“……That’s amazing…….”
As Jack lets out a gasp of surprise, Rudy asks him.
“Is this your first time in the Republic? You’re pretty fluent for someone who is.”
“Ah. It’s a bit of a coincidence, you see. I’ve actually studied the language a little…”
“Forget about the Republic—this is actually my first time even traveling abroad .”
Saying that, Jack gave a small chuckle.
“I actually like the atmosphere of this island. It’s a far cry from the United Kingdom.”
“……Specifically?”
Rudy furrows his brow and asks again.
Could it be that, in fact, in the United Kingdom—
I wonder if they’re interested in what lies beyond the island.
When asked about the differences between this island and the United Kingdom , Jack pauses to think before answering.
“First things first—the weather… It’s always raining in London, and the sky is dark.”
“Because the men are off at war, the women are now doing all the heavy lifting and whatever else needs to be done…”
“Because of the blackout, it gets pitch black at night. Everyone is terrified of air raids.”
Rudy stopped eating and listened intently.
“Um… Actually, when I was little, I went to London, too.”
“When I woke up this morning, the town was shrouded in fog, creating a mysterious atmosphere…”
“The department store sparkled, and as a child, I thought, ‘What a wonderful town this is.’”
“……Anything else?”
“A-anything else? Um….”
It seems Rudy is surprisingly interested, so I was prompted by ルディさん—
Jack and I kept talking about London and Paris the whole time we were eating.
After eating. Just as we were leaving the café, I decided to ask Mr. Jack.
“Mr. Jack, what are you going to do now?”
“Ah, well, about that…”
He furrows his brow in a troubled manner.
“I went all the way to Mirage, but there’s nothing in particular to do, and I’m just bored out of my mind.”
“I’m no stranger to entertainment for the wealthy, but at best, I’ll go for a walk or take a nap…”
Then, Rudy muttered, looking exasperated.
“……Even without spending any money, there’s plenty to see on this island.”
“Is that so? Well then, Rudy. Show me the way.”
“……I’m busy. The Director of the Administration Bureau isn’t idle enough to be acting as a tour guide for travelers.”
“Read the tourist guide or ask a hotel employee for more information.”
Rudy seems annoyed, but as for me…
How about having someone accompany you on your patrol?
I want to know what makes this island so charming…!
“So, how about having Mr. Jack accompany you on your patrol ?”
“That’s a great idea. If you’d like, why don’t you tell me about the island along the way ?”
“If it’s the kind of place you’d take a young lady, it shouldn’t be a problem if I come along, right?”
Jack is totally on board.
But Rudy just kept a stern look on his face.
“……Why do I have to go that far for Jack?”
“Oh, it was rude of me to ask for this for free, wasn’t it? I’m not exactly rolling in cash, but if it’s just a little…”
Seeing Jack’s nonchalant attitude, Rudy let out a sigh.
“……I get it. If you want to come along, go ahead and do whatever you want.”
“To begin with, the fact that an outsider is accompanying me is unusual, after all.”
“Even if there’s one more person, well… It won’t be a problem. I can handle whatever comes up.”
“I want to know about this island, too! Could you tell me about it…?”
Fleur d’Or is glamorous and beautiful— everywhere is wonderful.
But...
“I’d love to know what you find so charming about Rudy, who lives on the island! ”
“……I guess I have no choice.”
Rudy relented with a sigh.
“It’s a waste of time to argue about this, so do whatever you want.”
“Oh, thank you so much…!”
“To begin with, the fact that an outsider is accompanying me is unusual, after all.”
“Even if there’s one more person, well… It won’t be a problem. I can handle whatever comes up.”
“……Come to think of it, why are you, young lady, traveling with Rudy?”
“That is….”
I’m not sure how to explain this.
When I looked at Rudy as if to ask for help, he answered for me.
“She had relatives on the island. Because of that, the Administration Office is taking care of her during her stay.”
“Huh… That sounds pretty complicated.”
Did they sense that it was due to personal circumstances?
Jack nodded and didn’t press the matter any further.
That afternoon.
We accompanied Rudy on his patrol and visited various parts of Island.
Along the way, Fleur d’Or introduces magnificent architectural landmarks such as the opera house…
In Ecruse Ville, he took me to the farm on the forest side and the charming flower market, among other places.
Like buying seasonal flowers at places like this and decorating your home with them—
It might be wonderful to live that kind of life.
And before I knew it, time had flown by...
By the time I made it back to Vil Street, the sun was already beginning to set.
At that moment.
“……Sorry. I’ve got to run for a bit.”
With a brief word of farewell, Jack walked away from us.
Wondering what was going on, I followed his gaze to where he was heading…
There was a person crouching by the side of the road.
“Madam, are you all right?”
“Ah, my knee’s hurting a little…”
“I’ll walk you home. May I ask which way you’re going?”
“No, not at all… I’m so sorry. If I rest for a bit, I’ll be able to walk…”
To the elderly woman who is hesitant, he says gently.
“I can’t just leave a woman in trouble behind. I’m a man of the United Kingdom, after all.”
“We’re taught to be especially kind to children and the elderly.”
“Please let me help you.”
“Well then… Could you just carry my luggage for me?”
“Of course. If it’s not too much trouble, I’ll carry you and Madame …”
“Oh my. Please stop joking around.”
The old woman laughed, but I get the feeling Jack is actually quite serious about what he’s saying.
“……That’s amazing.”
The exchange was so swift and natural that Rudy and I found ourselves completely engrossed.
“Even though the islanders don’t usually trust travelers… To think they’d open up so easily…”
“You’re a kind person, aren’t you, Jack?”
“It’s not so much that I’m quick to win people over… I guess that’s a kind of talent, too.”
Jack, who had dropped off the old woman, and we met up again.
“I had a lot of fun today. Thanks, you two.”
“I had fun too…! Thank you, Rudy.”
“……I didn’t do anything special. I was just doing a routine check, you know.”
Just as he was saying that—
I could hear the anxious murmur of the crowd.
"What is that...?"
“……I wonder if something happened.”
Without hesitation, Rudy headed in that direction.
The wind carries the smell of something burning.
Pushing through the crowd, Rudy caught sight of what lay at the end of their gaze and held his breath.
“Is it… on fire…?”
Jack muttered, looking perplexed.
What people were watching was a raging, dancing ball of fire.
That is――
“Hmm…!”
A goat is being burned alive.
Desperate to escape the burning pain, he frantically thrashed about and writhed on the ground.
“Divide up and pass the water around!”
While I stood there dumbfounded, Rudy gave instructions to the others.
“Be very careful not to let the goat escape! The fire will spread.”
“Ah, ahh…!”
“Women and children, stay back. You never know where I’m going to strike.”
Jack says in a calm tone.
In that hand was a farming tool that he seemed to have borrowed from someone at some point.
Push the goat back so it can’t break through the circle of people, then splash the water you brought on it.
And then...
“Hey, Rudy?”
By the time the Administration Bureau agents, having heard the commotion, rushed to the scene—
The fire had already gone out.

I think, then ask.

The original book that everyone wants—one said to grant any wish.
Is it only natural that a scramble for control arises due to so many conflicting motives?

Right now, both the Republic and the United Kingdom are in the midst of war.

Serge is smiling as he looks at us.

My first day on this island.

en: “And yet… Who recommended me for Director? What were you thinking? Did you feel guilty or something?”
“……Well. I wonder.”
Serge lowered his gaze slightly.
When Rudy shows signs of frustration, he pulls out the original book and raises his voice.
“――Wind!”
The moment the rapier was swung down, a gust of wind was unleashed.

“Creates a vacuum with the wind to slice through enemies. It’s a spell formula that stays true to the basics.”
“Therefore, preventing it is easy. To break the vacuum, all you have to do is pump air into it.”
It’s just like being in a classroom—
He said this with a calm demeanor.
(Easier said than done…!)
Even someone like me, who’s only dabbled a little in magic, can understand this.
Just how difficult is it to actually do that?
“Well then….”
Suddenly, Sergei stroked the air with his fingertips, as if conducting an orchestra.
Just then—
A fierce wind begins to swirl.
“Huh!?”
Rudy immediately tried to resist his spell with his rapier, but—
A raging wind seized him, and his body was violently blown away.
“――Rudy-san!!”
I instinctively ran over to him as he collapsed.
“It’s all right――”
At that moment.
As if to cut off both my words and my movements, Rudy turned his palm toward me .
“……Don’t touch me.”
“B-but…!”
Without looking at me, he just glared at Serge—
Perhaps as a consequence of the original text, he stood up on his own two feet as if he felt no pain whatsoever.
Serge sighed and confronted him.
“……Let me answer that question from earlier.”
“To be precise, the reason I killed your mother was not due to personal feelings.”
“……What does that mean?”
“Didn’t I just mention that my promise was broken?”
“Did you know that back then, a military crisis arose following the Emperor of Time’s landing in a certain country?”
I’ve vaguely heard of it.
Long ago, <dic=206> various nations were locked in a standoff over </dic> a territory located in northwestern North Africa, it is said.
“To settle the matter quickly, the Republic has requested cooperation from this island.”
“I thought to myself: To stop this, I had no choice but to become the director myself.”
“……Did my mother know what would happen to mages who left the island ?”
“Is it because of that anger that never fades?” Rudy asked in a trembling voice.
With a smile that seems almost sad, Serge replies.
“Yes. I made several suggestions, though. She believed that, in order to protect the island, the sacrifice of the sorcerers was unavoidable.”
“They say that with great power comes great responsibility, don’t they? …Do you feel the same way?”
“I told you just now, didn’t I? …I want to protect the people I care about.”
“If that’s the sacrifice required, I’m prepared to make it.”
Rudy declared resolutely.
Although Serge’s voice is gentle, he responds in a firm tone.
“For me, that ‘necessary sacrifice’ is—”
“Your mother. The owner of the original book. And it meant killing an innocent child.”
“While you were serving as director and refusing conscription, the situation in a certain country changed, and the Republic withdrew its demand.”
“After that, I promoted tourism, and with the funds obtained from that, I secured a promise from the republican government to exempt the islanders from military service.”
He was betrayed by the island and sent to the battlefield in a situation where he was practically offered up as a sacrifice.
Why, then, do they still try to protect the island?
I didn’t know the answer to that.
But...
I’m sure there’s something important to Serge on this island.
"Shall we wrap up our conversation here?"
Serge held the materialized original book in one hand and once again traced the air with his fingertips.
It seems Rudy tried to block that wind using some kind of spell, but—
In a gust of wind even stronger than before , his entire body was sliced open in an instant, and he fell to his knees.
“Hmm…!”
Perhaps in response to my desire to help him?
The original book appeared right before my eyes.
“No, Aria!”
"No good, [主人公]!"
Rudy, who noticed this, raised his voice to stop him.
“I have the original book, too…!”
“Please let me help too!”
“I mean, you’re all bruised up like that…”
I don’t think I can fight any longer.
――If things stay this way, I’ll be killed.
An anxiety bordering on terror gripped my chest.
But...
He returned the rapier to the medallion, and without flinching in the slightest—
She stated it firmly in a composed voice.
“I told you I didn’t want to drag you into this. I—”
“When it comes to the one I love, I’ll do it on my own. …I want to protect them with my own hands…!”
He tried to stand up again, but his knees buckled immediately.
Even if I didn’t feel any pain , this isn’t just a superficial wound that would let me stand on my own.
But still...
His eyes had not lost their light.
Struggling with a body that won’t move as intended, I try to stand up again.
“……Rudy-san…….”
I could really feel his determination.
I shook off my hesitation, put the original book away—
I lean over him as he lies there and support his shoulder.
“! …Thank you.”
Until he stood up, Serge stood by and watched.
Rudy glared at him and declared firmly.
“I will avenge my mother, and then….”
“I’ll protect the people I care about—!”
I obtained the manifested original book.
“Write… Give me… power…!”
In response to those words, in the very next instant, a ferocious gale bursts forth from the original book.
In response, Serge also used the original book and created wind in the same way.
The wind roared and swirled――
“Hmm…!”
It was as if I were in the middle of a storm.
Their powers clash and rage.
No—
“Ugh…!”
I guess it really comes down to the difference in ability as a mage.
Gradually, Rudy begins to be pushed back.
(Please…!)
I stood by him and prayed.
Rudy desperately holds back the gale that threatens to tear our bodies apart.
But...
The clash of magical power generated by both sides—its aftermath bared its fangs as a blade.
Rudy’s body was sliced open as if cracking, and blood gushed out.
“Perhaps you should retreat. If you do so now, you’ll save your life.”
Serge’s body is also being torn apart at the edges by the wind, but…
Are the wounds less severe than Rudy’s?
He doesn’t seem the least bit intimidated.
……But the same goes for Rudy.
“There’s no way I’m backing down! I’m going to defeat you!”
Unbending in will, unbroken in spirit.
No matter how much blood I shed, I will keep fighting.
Serge slightly grimaced and let out a sigh.
Immediately afterward――
Rudy’s wind is rendered powerless as if it were being swallowed up by Serge’s wind.
A momentary lull fell over the space.
“Ah—”
Just when I thought it was all over...
“……Guh, ……gah……”
――Suddenly, Serge coughed up blood.
“Huh…?”
It was a sudden ending.
Didn’t you realize your own limitations?
As he collapsed as if a string had snapped, he let out a raspy voice.
“……Is this as far as it goes……?”
“……My apologies. I’m afraid I’ve shown you something rather unsightly . My body is starting to fall apart.”
That statement was, in fact, the unvarnished truth.
Just by looking at his ashen face, I understood immediately.
He slowly moves his lips.
It was the voice a person mustered with their last breath.
“……To protect what I want to protect…… I just don’t want to make the people I care about sacrifice themselves……”
“So… I’d say the current Rudy is actually pretty good, I think….”
As soon as he uttered those words, his upper body swayed—
Serge collapsed right there.
“……I don’t want to hear you say things like that.”
Standing before the lifeless corpse, he murmurs.
There was no longer any anger in that expression.
After that...
Testimonies from the Hotel staff. Documents left behind at Serge’s house.
After scrutinizing these, the Administration tracked his plan and his movements.
――Results.
There was no sign that he had contacted anyone; rather, it became clear that he had been avoiding people.
The more I investigate, the more evidence I find suggesting it’s confirmed that he was acting alone.
He had previously said that an important promise to the country and the island had been broken.
That’s why I didn’t trust anyone—
Or maybe I just couldn’t trust it anymore .
The Administration continues to investigate the black-haired man who tried to take the original book from me, as well as his accomplices.
The reason why Yuris was killed remains unknown.
It seems that quite a few sorcerers, scheming to get their hands on the original book, were lurking on the island…
Now that the original texts have all been gathered in one place, perhaps they’ve become unable to move.
While Rudy and the Administration Bureau continued their vigilance and investigation, they were coming to that conclusion.
On the other hand, some new facts have also come to light.
Apparently, a bullet from the gun owned by Mei was found in the decomposing corpse discovered in the forest.
Thanks to the treatment, he woke up safely According to Mr. Percy...
They were attacked by a suspicious person, but they managed to fend him off.
As a result, he unexpectedly obtained the original book and used its power to conceal the corpse.
……And then.
One day, as the festival was nearing its end.
A report came in to the Administration Bureau.
“Hello, Director and Mademoiselle. How have you been?”
“T-That’s my line…!”
Right before our eyes――
Charles Paradille, who had been missing for the past eight days, has finally reappeared.
Thanks to this, the opera house is in a frenzy.
It’s much noisier than when people gather to watch a play.
“……Are you hurt? I was sure you’d been killed by someone, or maybe even kidnapped.”
“Fortunately, I’m not hurt. It’s just….”
Charles smiled gently, then revealed a shocking truth.
“Your guess is pretty much spot on. I was unfortunately abducted and held captive for a while.”
“I-Is that so…!?”
“It seems someone I have a history with was on the island … I was held up there.”
“I couldn’t escape for quite a while, so I helplessly waited for help .”
“I wonder if they gave up too? The restraints suddenly disappeared, so I just walked out on my own.”
Charles, looking somewhat dazed, smiled at us.
“If you guys had the original book, I wish you’d come to my rescue sooner.”
“! Why did you do that…?”
“Of course, that’s because I heard you guys talking about it at the abandoned church in the forest .”
Charles answers confidently.
“Is that…?”
――Is this about what happened back then?
Rudy asks with a puzzled look.
“No way… Were you trapped in that place? I didn’t sense anything like that, though….”
“I could say it was that place, or I could say it wasn’t . A gap between dimensions, perhaps—I was on the other side, just a hair’s breadth away from this world .”
“It was like getting lost in a fairy-tale land— a truly rare experience.”
Rudy’s expression tenses up slightly.
“……To think you understand that situation so precisely… So, that means you’re a mage too—”
“Shh.”
He cut her off briefly and brought his index finger to his lips.
“I’m a mysterious chansonier from Montmartre. Please don’t pursue this. I won’t cause any trouble for the Director.”

“Um…”

“‘The restraints disappeared today,’ that’s what Charles said, right?”
“Why is that…?”
“……Since it’s a rather unique and advanced spell, maybe it’s reached its limit in terms of maintenance.”
“Or maybe the situation has changed, and I’ve decided to step back this year.”

“Why are you looking so serious— …Ah, there’s no need to worry, right?”
“I was dozing off , half-asleep, so I didn’t hear what you guys were talking about in the abandoned church.”
“Whether it was saying ‘Mademoiselle is cute’ or saying ‘I’ll miss you when we part,’ rest assured—I have absolutely no idea what any of that means.”
“Huh!?”

The moment I thought that.

I think Jack is a sincere person.

“I’m sorry, but this is beyond my capabilities.”

“……It’s not entirely impossible, I suppose.”
He nodded casually, still smiling.
“This boundary might be fragile enough to break at the slightest provocation.”
“Because we wished for it in the original book… Surely now, it’s as if the dream is lasting just a little longer.”
“Ahès said this is the bottom of the sea, a phantom city.”
“Ahès?”
“Oh. I’m the girl who was with Rudy and the others back then.”
Evan lowered his eyes as if deep in thought and exhaled softly.
“If it’s just an illusion at the bottom of the sea, it’ll be over in an instant. There’s no point in that.”
“……What I want is the real thing—the kind that can’t be lost.”
He clenches his fist on his lap.
“Once I return to my original world, I’ll get my younger brother back I’ll find another way—”
“It’s not that it’s incomplete—I’m just thinking I want to find the right way.”
Is there a way to do that?
Of course, I hope Evan’s wish comes true …
“Now then, Miss Lapraud. Make a wish upon the original book.”
Prompted, I turn to the original text.
“……Please send us back to our original world.”
After being enveloped in a blinding light.
Before I knew it, I was standing on Vil Street.
I recognize the scene of the cathedral being crowded with people returning to Fleur d’Or.
“As expected of Mirage, that was a ceremony with real atmosphere.”
“Wow, I got totally sucked in without even realizing it.”
(It’s the first day of the festival…!)
And so――
We have welcomed the start of the festival for the third time.
Last night...
After confirming that the lights were off at Grandma’s house, I returned to the Hôtel Azur.
In the room I was shown on the day I arrived on this island, my luggage was there—just as I remembered.
And then, the next morning...
After finishing breakfast early, I waited for Evan at the reception desk.
On the first day of the festival, I’m sure I met him here.
(……It should be coming, right?)
I wonder if Evan remembers what happened between us.
The longer I wait, the more anxious I get.
Then—
“Good morning, Ms. Lapraud.”
“! Good morning……”
Evan appeared.
You can’t tell just from a greeting how much he remembers.
But what should I ask?
While I’m at a loss for words due to nervousness, Evan says.
“I want to learn more about this island.”
“I’m thinking of heading to the Portail Bleu library next…”
“Would you help me out too? …Like you used to.”
“Y-yes! Of course…!”
They know about the library, even though they shouldn’t have known about it yet.
We’ve even walked there together.
(Just like me...)
(It’s Evan, back from the bottom of the sea.)
Evan and I walk together through the streets of Fleur d’Or.
“Just collecting the original books won’t make our wishes come true. This is a major discovery.”
“I’m sure there’s a trick to making wishes. It’s hard, isn’t it?”
In a casual tone, as if making small talk, he talks about what lies ahead.
“But I was able to confirm that a mysterious power definitely exists on this island.”
“……Rather than relying on the power of the original text, I wonder if I can find a way to grant wishes by utilizing the traits themselves.”
“For example… what kind of method?”
He answers my question with a smile.
“I have absolutely no idea. For now, it’s like grasping at clouds.”
“What must I do to make my wish come true? I must find that method—one that surely no one knows yet.”
“For the third festival, I plan to spend my time with the intention of reading every single document in Portail Blue.”
“……You’re very optimistic, Evan.”
Even though I’ve just returned from a dream world where I thought my dream had finally come true.
He doesn’t seem the least bit down.
He smiles as he looks at me, who is a little confused.
“If you’ll help me look for clues, I have a feeling we’ll figure something out.”
“Personally, luck hasn’t really been on my side so far …”
“! I’m confident in my luck.”
When I told him that, he nodded as if he understood.
“……You’re really lucky.”
“So that’s how it is, after all? Without having to fight over the third book I’d been thinking, just a little, that maybe it was thanks to you that I happened to get my hands on it by chance.”
“I hope so, though…”
I want to be of help to him.
……But a slight sense of unease flits through my mind.
(This person is the Evan I know.)
Even though we’ve only known each other for a short time, I feel that his strong curiosity and desire to explore the unknown are very much in character for him.
But...
(I feel like I might be a little too optimistic...)
Maybe I’m just trying too hard to act cheerful .
Although I thought that, it didn’t seem like mere bluster ……
However, it feels as though their true feelings are being hidden.
Only a strange sense of unease lingered in my heart.
Then we arrived at the Administration Office.
Visiting this place together with you feels somehow nostalgic, and it makes me a little happy.
“...So, I’d like to use the library here .”
Yuris blinked , seemingly surprised by the candid offer.
“You sure know your stuff… I didn’t realize the Administration Bureau had a library open to the public.”
“Well, since there aren’t many users, we don’t actually have a librarian here.”
Without probing further, Yuris led us to the library.
“Please use this normally within the bounds of common sense. Oh, and please don’t take the book out of the store, okay?”
After offering just a brief reminder, he left the library immediately, just as he had before.
“……Well then, let’s get right to reading it.”
"Yes!"
We set aside the book we had just finished reading and began reading the reference material.
I glanced at Evan, who was sitting in the chair next to me.
He was engrossed in reading the book with a serious expression.
Even though I feel a vague sense of unease, I can’t bring myself to say anything.
“……Many of this island’s mysterious powers and phenomena are caused by Sirene’s power.”
When I looked up from the book.
I couldn’t quite make out Evan’s expression.
“Only during the festival season does Sirene…”
“It might not be a siren, but anyway.”
“It is said that the god who sleeps in this land will appear and bestow power upon the people.”
"Yes."
I remember something he told me before.
“The story goes that the god of this land wasn’t originally Sirene— perhaps they were called by a different name .”
“Siren… if you looked into that god a little more…”
“Do you know anything about the original book?”
"Maybe."
Evan nodded.
“However, it seems that no accurate legends have been passed down on this island.”
“Although the islanders all believe that the god of Mirage is ‘Siren’—”
“It seems you don’t know exactly what that is, though.”
“! That’s true…”
Now that you mention it, it might be a strange story.
Most gods appearing in mythology have their own distinct personalities.
Titles such as “God of Abundance,” “God of Art,” and “God of War.”
Then, things like what they like or dislike. How they behaved toward others.
In most cases, a “story” based on that divinity is included.
(In Mirage, you don’t hear that…)
Sirène “bestows blessings”—
That’s all that’s mentioned in any of the references.
“If only her background, past titles, and anecdotes had been passed down…”
“It would make it easier to get closer to the true nature of the god ‘Sirene’ , though…”
I checked late into the night, but I couldn’t possibly expect to get any results right away……
We returned to the hotel.
“Well then, good night. See you tomorrow.”
“Good night, Evan.”
“See you tomorrow.”
We hadn’t made any specific promises, but as if it were a given—
I realized we were planning to meet at the same place and at the same time as always.
Evan, who broke up with me, heads toward the casino instead of taking the elevator.
Come to think of it, something like that happened before, too.
(It might be for socializing, not just for betting.)
Whether it’s Finn or the people at the séance, I realize now that he actually has quite a few acquaintances—more than I would have expected.
I’ll ask about this next time I get the chance.
After seeing him off, I head toward the elevator.
At that moment.
“You’re such a bad girl, out so late, aren’t you, Mine Schatz?”
I was so surprised I was at a loss for words.
“Sha… Mr. Charles…!”
Of course, in this world, they’re very much alive.
A small sense of joy and relief welled up at this realization, and I breathed a sigh of relief.
“……Is something wrong?”
He senses my unease and asks me about it.
“N-no, anything…!”
“It was so sudden that I was just surprised.”
“Hmm……”
He raised one eyebrow and stared at me.
“Hey, have you been lured away by something evil?”
“Huh…?”
It was a strangely meaningful phrase.
Wanting to know his true intentions, I looked back at him, and he smiled gently and continued speaking.
“There are various rumors about Mirage. …Among them are stories of people vanishing without a trace.”
"If you carelessly step into the wrong place, you might not be able to get back."
Staring blankly, leaving me behind――
Charles walked away with a dashing air.
Pressing my hand to my pounding chest, I watched ’s retreating figure.
I know I’m probably overthinking this, but…
It felt as if our actions up to that point had been seen right through.
Returning to my room, I slumped listlessly onto the bed.
Nights spent alone are lonely.
And to think I’d forgotten all about that these past few years.
(Dad……)
I recall a fleeting dream, and it makes my heart ache.
Even so, I can’t bring my dad back from the dead.
That was a wish that defied the laws of the world— a wish that must never be granted.
Looking back on my past choices, that’s what I think.
(But Evan is……)
He still holds onto the wish to get his younger brother back and reunite with his family.
I can’t say I don’t understand how he feels.
But...
(I wonder if that’s really okay……)
I still can’t get my thoughts in order.
I let out a sigh all by myself.
Today, once again, we’re heading to the library.
On my way to a café for lunch, I spotted Jack there.
“Hey, young lady. …Have you gotten closer to that gentleman over there since then?”
I feel a sense of nostalgia for words I’ve heard before.
“Thank you for your concern.”
“Evan has been teaching me all sorts of things about the island.”
“Huh….”
Seeing him look a little surprised, Evan introduced himself—
Just like that time, the three of us ended up having lunch together.
“Come to think of it, I heard there are fairies in the United Kingdom . Is that true?”
“If you don’t mind, I’d love to hear a story about fairies.”
“A fairy is… a being that exists somewhere between a human and a god.”
“In terms of wielding the power of nature, I guess I’m kind of like a witch.”
“They’re pranksters, but you don’t want to make them angry. They’re a cruel bunch who’ll turn people into toys in a heartbeat.”
Now that I’ve gained knowledge of changelings, those words sounded very heavy.
“Well, there are some friendly ones out there, but it’s best not to get involved.”
“<dic=316> Seely Court </dic> and <dic=107> Unseely Court </dic>, right? Friendly fairies and hostile fairies.”
“……For the people of the United Kingdom, fairies are a very familiar presence, aren’t they?”
“We are neighbors, after all. Separated by the world, though.”
“But we mustn’t forget that we humans and fairies live in different worlds.”
I nodded, as if savoring the moment.
“Um, are there fairies in the city, too?”
“Ah. Ms. Lapraud has been to London , hasn’t she?”
“I suppose there are some… but aren’t there more in the countryside ?”
“Ireland is a common example.”
“Scotland, Wales… Is the rest Cornwall?”
I try to visualize a map in my head, but I can only make out the rough spatial relationships.
“It’s said that Celtic influences still run deep in that area .”
“The Brittany region, to which this island belongs, is also part of the Celtic cultural sphere.”
“So, what exactly is ‘Celt’…?”
I’ve heard that name before.
However, I didn’t know the exact definition.
“A people who flourished in ancient times, and parts of their culture continue to this day.”
“To put it simply, the people who believe in God are different from us.”
“They do not follow the teachings of the church, but cherish what they have passed down through their traditions.”
A unique culture that has endured to this day.
Perhaps the same could be said for the Sirene faith in Mirage.
After lunch, we returned to Portail Bleu for the afternoon.
As soon as we enter the building, we spot the Director of the Administration Bureau.
“Hello, Rudy.”
When I speak to him, he returns my gaze with a look of wariness.
“I hear you guys have been hanging out in our library a lot lately?”
“Right. I want to learn about this island’s history.”
Evan smiles and replies.
“I’m researching folklore. I’m interested in local traditions, myths, and how they came to be.”
“In particular, I’m very drawn to the Sirene faith on this island.”
Rudy frowned as if it were a hassle.
“……It’s just a customary practice for the islanders, so there’s really nothing worth mentioning.”
“Uh, um. During the festival, we decorate with Cronne, and burn it on the last day, right?”
“……You know a lot about this. You’ve been spending every day in the library —it doesn’t look like you’re getting any sleep.”
“The crown of the cathedral is made using traditional methods with otogirigusa and mistletoe branches.”
“On the final day of the festival, there’s also a ritual where you burn it and offer it to Sirene.”
“Well, I guess that’s one of the main features of this island’s festival.”
In what year, exactly, did the Sirene faith begin on this island?
I couldn’t find any literature that clearly documented its origin, though…
Evan found a description that might serve as a clue.
“It seems that the momentum for the Sirene faith particularly surged in 1666.”
Evan held out the book he had been reading so that I could see it.
“It seems the Black Death, which had been plaguing the islanders at that time, has finally come to an end.”
“! The Black Death……”
A terrifying plague that occasionally breaks out on a large scale.
“……So people accepted the end of the Black Death as a miracle of Sirène, didn’t they?”
“And it seems they’ve demolished the old church and begun building a new cathedral to serve as the island’s symbol.”
Suddenly realizing this, I point to the illustration in the book.
“It is customary to decorate the cathedral with Cronnes and offer them at the end of the festival— ”
“Did this start around this time?”
“……It seems so. The methods and ritual procedures appear to be carefully preserved as well.”
Detailed instructions on the plants used for Cronne and how to weave them are provided .
"Use this tree for the main structure, and these flowers and plants for decoration," and so on.
“Hmm…?”
Evan’s gaze fell on a passage somewhere, and he furrowed his brow as he sank into deep thought.
“Why is this…? No…”
What on earth did I find?
His expression gradually grew more serious.
“Evan…?”
I tentatively called out to them, but there was no response.
Tracing the text in the book with his finger, he muttered as if possessed by something.
“To begin with, I felt something was off about holding the Summer Solstice Festival in the first place…”
“This island has a warm climate. If you’re praying for a bountiful harvest, the May Festival should be enough…”
“Uh, um…!”
“Evan, what’s wrong? What did you find out……?”
When I called out to him desperately, he let out a long sigh.
“……I’ve been thinking about this in my own way these past few days.”
“Even though I gathered all three volumes and prayed to the original book, my wish wasn’t exactly granted, was it?”
“Y-yes…”
“The entity known as Sirene and is the one manifesting that original text.”
“In other words, is it strange to think that Sirène has more power than the original book? ”
Now that you mention it, you’re right.
If one is capable of creating the original work, they would likely possess abilities beyond that.
“In other words, what I’m thinking is—”
“The idea is to use the original text as a starting point and try having a direct conversation with Sirene.”
“A conversation? With God…?”
"Yeah."
He nodded, but I couldn’t quite grasp it.
“Let’s talk… What are you going to do?”
“That really depends on the other person, I guess. I think I’ll just let things take their course.”
“Huh…?”
A cry of bewilderment escaped him.
However, for some reason, Evan seems to have unwavering confidence.
“After all, the gods spoken of in many legends are surprisingly capricious —they’ll grant people’s wishes.”
“W-well, I’ve definitely heard something like that before, though….”
“Even if I could talk to Sirene, there’s no guarantee she’d grant my wish, right?”
“If this is seen as disrespectful, it might anger the gods…”
“You know a lot, don’t you?”
For some reason, Evan smiled contentedly.
“It’s generally the norm that they sometimes demand a price from the other party in exchange for granting a wish.”
“But gods really are moody. I think it’s worth meeting and talking to one, don’t you?”
Since a professor of folklore says so, there must be some basis for it.
But...
“The price to be paid might actually be surprisingly easy to pay.”
“Don’t you think it’s worth a try rather than giving up right from the start?”
I nodded vaguely.
This sounds like such a far-fetched story that I find it hard to wholeheartedly agree.
“Is that even possible…?”
“We’ll have to think about that later and just keep working to improve the accuracy as much as possible.”
Evan smiled happily.
“Will you help me, too?”
I feel a fair amount of responsibility toward him.
It was me who brought Evan—who was content with that world—back to this side.
As they looked at me with eyes full of expectation, I hesitated……
Of course!
……Depends on the method
"Of course!"
I accepted the job without hesitation.
If I can be of help to the people I care about, I’ll do my very best.
“Thanks, that really helps.”
Evan’s expression softens slightly, but he looks pleased.
“……It depends on the method……”
I couldn’t answer right away.
A sense of unease—or perhaps something like fear—has been constantly haunting me.
Evan didn’t seem discouraged; instead, he nodded as if he understood.
“That’s true. I’ll have to find a way to do this without you objecting.”
As I gazed at him, I murmured to myself.
(I don’t know if Evan’s wish will come true, though……)
(I hope the sadness he’s been carrying all this time will be eased, even just a little...)
I hope his prayers are answered.
……That’s what I thought.
Evan and I had been holed up in the Portail Bleu library since that morning as well.
Late afternoon. We visit the Fleur d’Or café for a meal.
“When I’m reading a book, I can forget about being hungry, but once my concentration breaks, I’m completely lost.”
Several dishes are lined up in front of him.
For example, a dish featuring slow-simmered aromatic vegetables and lobster.
Dieppe-style flounder with a rich wine flavor. Chicken from Bresse, stuffed with truffles and roasted.
His appetite was as hearty as ever today, and the food on his plate was disappearing before his very eyes.
(He’s a big eater...)
<dic=225> While carefully eating the piping-hot gratin from Coquille Saint-Jacques </dic> —
I find myself thinking that once again this time.
“This flounder has such a rich flavor… That’s Mirage for you.”
“Even in a simple café like this, the food tastes just as good as in a Parisian restaurant.”
“……Oh, the chicken is delicious, too. It’s tender, and it really has a nice truffle aroma.”
Seeing him speak with such enthusiasm, I couldn’t help but laugh along.
“Evan, you sure do eat with such an appetite, don’t you?”
“I don’t know about that, though…”
“Would you like to try some, Ms. Lapraud?”
“Huh! I-is that okay?”
I’ve eaten things Evan doesn’t like on his behalf before.
“Really? Yeah. Since we’re at it, it’d be better if you enjoyed eating it, right?”
“It would be unfair to the person who made this to just leave it as is, so I’d really appreciate it if you could help me……”
Over the past few days, I’ve been watching him up close as he plays the role of the reliable “Professor,” but…
In this regard, it remains innocent, so to speak.
I can’t help but think, “What a cute person.”
That said, my feelings toward him are a little different now than they were back then.
Maybe Evan doesn’t mean anything by it.
But...
Maybe Evan doesn’t mean anything by it.
But...
“Here, open wide.”
I get flustered by advances from someone I like.
(This wasn’t here before…!)
For Evan and me, this is our third festival.
Since they both have memories of the past, it’s only natural that even if they act the same way, the details will differ… but still.
My heart was pounding from nervousness and embarrassment.
“……I wonder if they’re not going to eat it?”
“I-I’ll dig in…!”
Summoning my courage, I ate the bite-sized piece of chicken he offered me.
“It’s delicious, isn’t it?”
“Uh… y-yes….”
I can barely manage to nod back at him as he smiles.
I’m completely at the mercy of Mr. Evan.
Even though you know I like him.
I think it’s sneaky to do something like this while acting like it’s no big deal.
“……Uh, excuse me.”
Trying to hide my embarrassment, I bring up the topic.
“Evan, in order to talk to Sirène, you’re planning to collect the original books first, right?”
“What… are you planning to do about that?”
“What do you mean, ‘how’?”
What exactly is being asked?
He tilted his head, looking as if he had no idea what was going on.
“……If we don’t do anything, the day after tomorrow.”
“Finn is attacked by someone, and they both end up killed, causing the third original book to fall onto the sandy beach.”
……Um, I was attacked by a monster.
Tormented by pain, he dies in despair.
“To someone… Ah. You were at the bottom of the sea and actually witnessed what happened with your own eyes, didn’t you?”
In the end, I couldn’t do anything over there.
When I think back on that night, the fear still comes flooding back.
And the guilt he felt for letting him die also never faded.
“I… don’t want to let Finn die .”
“Um, the person attacking him, too.”
“It might be difficult, but I was wondering if there’s a way we could get through this without either of us dying …”
Evan gave a wry smile.
“I understand how you feel. …But I still need to get my hands on the original book.”
“Is there any way to save the two of them and get the original book as well…?”
Evan narrowed his eyes.
As if looking at something rare, he watches me for a while .
He looked like he was about to say, “You sure do like to make things complicated,” but…
It didn’t seem like they were exasperated or annoyed.
“……I know what’s going to happen, and I don’t think there’s anything I can’t handle.”
Has he come to a conclusion?
Evan took a sip of apple wine, smiled, and continued.
“After all, we have two copies of the original book.”
After dinner, we returned to the Administration Office once again.
When we entered the building, it was as if it had known we were coming —
“……We’ve met again, haven’t we…….”
Ahès stood there alone.
“……We’ve met again, haven’t we…….”
“Hello, Ahès.”
After greeting her as she gave a small smile, I told Evan.

To my girlfriend, who’s worried about me, I—

I can’t put it into words any further than that.

I don’t think I know the specifics, but I might be sensing something.
