“……Thank you so much for teaching me all this.”
“……See you later, Ahès.”
“Hmm…”
After saying goodbye to them.
I hurried up to the second floor.
Enter the library quietly.
He seems completely engrossed in his book and shows no sign of noticing me.
(Evan knows more about fairies and changeling folklore than I do...)
Folklore—his area of expertise.
On top of that, given the situation with your younger brother , you must have checked it especially thoroughly.

“Huh? Is that right, Aria?”
“Huh? Is that right, [主人公]?”
“Oh, yes. The day after the festival’s final day is actually my 20th birthday.”
But...
“Did I really tell Leon that much …?”
“Oh, I’ve heard that. On the ship, right?”
(Was that right…?)
I have absolutely no recollection of this.
Between how I ended up on this island and everything else that’s been happening, I’m starting to worry about my memory.
“But, I see. Bambina, you see…”
“Oh… So it’s your birthday…”
Mei and Charles are both repeatedly nodding as if something is going on .
There—
“There you are, Aria-chan!”
“There you are, [主人公]-chan!”
“Oh, the Administration Bureau…”
It was Yuris who spoke to me.
He ran over and smiled sheepishly.
“Sorry for bringing this up so soon after yesterday. Actually, about your house …”
“Oh, to be precise, ‘about Grandma’s house,’ right? …Actually, I found a broken window this morning.”
“Since it could be a thief, I was wondering if you could be there as a witness, just in case.”
“……I understand.”
I nodded nervously.
“That’s tough…”
“Ma chérie. Please, let everything go smoothly.”
“Yes… Thank you.”
Being called “Ma Chéri” was a bit strange to me, deep down…
I appreciate Charles’ thoughtfulness.
Then, Leon says something unexpected.
“……Well then, I’ll come along too.”
“! Are you sure?”
“Of course. You must be worried that I might be a thief. Besides, I was planning to spend the day with you anyway.”
In front of Grandma’s house, Rudy’s figure was standing.
“We’d like you to join us in inspecting the room .”
“Even if something was stolen, I’m sure you wouldn’t know… but for now, let’s at least check the situation together.”
"Yes. Please do."
After explaining that much, Rudy glanced briefly at Leon and furrowed his brow.
“……So, why is Leon Vitry with us?”
“It’s kind of like a guardian. You’d be worried about letting a girl go to a crime scene all by herself, wouldn’t you?”
Rudy looks at me with a puzzled expression.
“Y-yes. They kindly offered to help.”
“……Well, if you’re okay with it, I guess that’s fine……”
And then—using the key I’d been given, I opened the door to Grandma’s house.
“A neighbor who heard the sound of a window breaking says that right after that, they saw children running away as if fleeing.”
“Huh. …I wonder if he used to play soccer?”
“Soccer… Oh, you mean football.”
Now that you mention it—
Yesterday……
On the street in front of Grandma’s house, I saw some children playing.
“Just to be sure, were there any signs that anyone had entered the room ?”
“As far as I could tell, that didn’t seem to be the case. The key is still there, and above all, a window is a window, right?”
Rudy points to the broken window.
“……There’s no way to get into the house from here, is there?”
The window had metal bars on it.
Even a child wouldn’t be allowed inside.
“No signs of a crime, huh? …So, you really did call her just to identify her and explain the situation, didn’t you?”
“……I’m relieved.”
I breathe a sigh of relief.
“……Anyway, you’d like to get that window fixed, right? If you’d like, I can arrange for a contractor.”
“! Please help.”
There’s no way I can just leave Grandma’s house out in the open like that .
Mr. Rudy promised that the Administration Bureau would find the culprit and make them reimburse the repair costs.
And then...
I was using a broom to clean up the glass.
Rudy is using a dustpan, and is helping him with it.
Meanwhile, Leon leaned against the wall and watched the cleaning go on.
“……Oh, there’s one over there, too.”
"Thank you."
“……Monsieur Vitré, you’ve been all talk this whole time, haven’t you?”
“I don’t usually clean up after myself. What should I do…?”
“Hehe…”
I crouch down while listening to what they have to say.
Since the shard was surprisingly large, I tried to pick it up with my hand instead of using a broom—
A slight pain shot through my fingertips.
Was I not careful enough? I cut the pad of my finger on some glass.
――A single drop of that blood falls at your feet.
Suddenly, light poured forth as if rising from the floor.
The moment that happened, a warmth spread through my chest.
Something unidentifiable races beneath my skin.
Faced with an unfamiliar sensation I’d never felt before, my breath caught in my throat.
And then――
“Whoa!?”
“A sudden burst of magical power…!?”
It felt like something had snapped.
Before I knew it, a strange book had materialized right in front of me.
“! That’s….”
Leon lets out a cry of astonishment.
At that moment, a certain image came to mind—
(What about the current one…?)
What on earth happened?
Still unsure, I picked up the book in front of me.
“Uh… Wait a second. Too many things are happening all at once.”
“……Is everything okay? Any pain, dizziness, or anything like that……?”
“Y-yes…”
Not knowing how to explain it and unable to find the right words, he nodded vaguely.
“……I think it’s probably okay……”
At that moment.
Leon spoke, sounding a bit flustered.
“……Everyone. Just a moment ago, in a place like that … Was there something like that there?”
When I looked in the direction I was told to...
――A small door, glowing faintly, had appeared in a corner of the room.
“Oh, it wasn’t there…!”
Just a few seconds ago, this was supposed to be just a wall.
“……A moment ago, the floor glowed, didn’t it? At that moment, I felt magic at work. Probably—”
“I think the magic that had been hiding the door all this time was broken because it reacted to her… Lapraado’s blood.”
“Magic…? You mean… magic…?”
After some hesitation, Rudy opened his mouth with a pained expression.
“……Broadly speaking, that understanding is correct. There are many people on this island with a natural aptitude for magic, and they learn how to use it from a young age.”
I was so surprised I couldn’t even speak.
Meanwhile, Leon shows no sign of surprise as he listens to our conversation.
“So, whoever was hiding this door was….”
“That’s your grandmother, of course. She was a famous sorceress.”
“The Laplard family has produced outstanding mages for generations.”
I stood silently in front of the door—
I want to open it
This is kind of scary……
(……I want to open it)
What kind of room lies ahead?
I just can’t stop being curious.
(This is kind of scary...)
What was hidden behind that mysterious door?
A fear of the future welled up in my heart.
“……Aria.”
"Yes."
Called by name in an urgent tone, I nod.
Feeling my heart pounding loudly, I gently place my hand on the door—
The door opened effortlessly.
Looking around the room, Leon says.
“……It feels like a witch’s workshop. Oh, I don’t mean that in a bad way, though.”
I’ve been here before.
“Okay? Aria. First, you need to learn how to handle magic.”
“Got it? [主人公]. First, you need to learn how to handle magic.”
“What’s ‘marikyoku’…?”
“The power to make the invisible visible.”
“Or perhaps it is your life force—and your blood itself.”
“When you encounter a problem for the first time, observe it first.”
“Sight, hearing, smell… Use your five senses to accurately grasp what is happening right before your eyes.”
"To use magic 'well,' knowledge and experience are essential."
“Aria doesn’t have either yet.”
“Neither is present in ‘[主人公]’ yet.”
“That’s exactly why it’s so important to be prepared.”
“If you can handle it with what you have on hand, that’s the most efficient magic.”
“During this island’s festival, Sirene’s blessings sometimes manifest in tangible form.”
“It is called the ‘Original Book’—”
(……Wait, what did you just say……)
(Was I learning magic from Grandma right here…?)
I stood there in a daze.
Before I could sort through my overwhelming memories, Rudy cut in.
“……About that book. It’s called the ‘original text.’”
“Just now, using your blood as a medium, Grandmother’s magic circle—the magic was activated.”
“The remnants of her magical power surged into you all at once, and you nearly caused a magical backlash.”
“Well, I was about to wake him up—actually, I had already woken him up—and Rudy and I managed to subdue him, though.”
I was doing my best to keep up with my own changes, but…
It seems I was being helped without even realizing it.
As if to say, “Don’t say anything unnecessary,” Rudy glared at Yuris in silence.
Don’t you notice that gaze?
Yuris continued without seeming to mind.
“Was the manifestation of the original book also triggered by an accidental explosion? Or did you try to bring it out yourself?”
Leon says this with a look of complexity on his face.
“It sounds like a pretty outlandish story, though…”
“This is the legendary Mirage. When it comes to magic, it wouldn’t be surprising if anything happened.”
As I search my memory, I awkwardly verify.
“……This original book……”
“……That’s the form of Sirene’s blessing, isn’t it?”
Were my words unexpected?
In particular, they gasped in surprise.
“My grandmother taught me that. …I just remembered.”
“The claim that it grants any wish isn’t a lie by any means, but…”
“Remember this well, Aria.”
“Remember this well, [主人公].”
“That is something that drives people mad—for better or worse.”
“Power that is too great corrupts the human spirit. The owner’s character isn’t strong enough to withstand that demonic nature.”
“However, if the owner has the right aptitude, the impact will be minimal.”
“……Don’t you understand? ……I see. Maybe it was a little too soon for Aria.”
“……Don’t you know? ……I see. [主人公]—maybe it was a little too soon.”
“When using the original book, humans must pay a very heavy price.”
“Just remember this one thing. The price you’ll pay is――…….”
“You’d forgotten all this until now, but did you suddenly remember so many things all at once ?”
“I wonder if that’s also due to the misfire… No, I’m probably overthinking it…”
Yuris tilted her head and fell deep in thought.
“So the original book drives people crazy, huh… Logically speaking, I can kind of see why.”
“There are certain things humans understand. It’s common for people who suddenly come into a lot of money to start acting strangely, isn’t it?”
“……I think there’s a more magical basis to it, though. In fact, owning the original book might actually lead to breaking free from the shackles of reason.”
I gaze at the original book in my hands.
“Just remember this,” my grandmother urged me—
“……The original book says that, as a price, it takes away the things that person cherishes.”
“I knew about the existence of the ‘price’ myself, but… That person had actually figured out the details as well.”
Rudy pondered for a moment, then made a suggestion.
“……I’d like to check the documents here. There might be things written here about the island that even we don’t know.”
“……That person didn’t belong to the Administration Bureau either; all alone , they’d been investigating something all along.”
“Does that mean the Administration is going to launch an investigation?”
“No, speaking for myself. I don’t want to be part of a crowd rummaging through what that person left behind.”
His words revealed his thoughtfulness.
I’ve heard that Rudy knew my grandmother when she was alive.

en: ……I think I can trust him with this.
“……Please, Rudy.”
When I answered that, he nodded as if relieved.
The original book of Mirage, which is said to grant a wish when you collect all three volumes...
Rudy warned me that possessing it would likely entail some danger.
After receiving instructions on what to do next, by the time I stepped outside, the sun had already set.
After saying goodbye to Rudy and heading home.
“……Um, Leon.”
I look up at him walking beside me and ask.
“I just remembered something…”
“Didn’t we meet on this island when we were little?”
Is it because the sunset is so bright?
He narrowed his eyes slightly and nodded.
“……That’s right. Since you seem to have forgotten —I didn’t tell you, but I met you 13 years ago.”
“I knew it…!”
There are still some ambiguous parts, though...
At that moment, the image that flashed through my mind for an instant seems to have been a memory from the past.
“If you’ve remembered, just call me Leon, like back then.”
“Huh? But….”
Since then, we’ve grown up.
He has become the CEO of a major global corporation.
“Since we’ve finally reunited, don’t hold back. You don’t need to use honorifics either.”
“……Well then…….”
“……Leon.”
When I hesitantly called him that, he smiled happily.
The next morning. At the reception desk, Serge stopped me.
“Are you all right? I heard yesterday that Marie—your grandmother’s house—was burglarized…”
“Oh, no! It seems the kids were playing and just broke the window.”
“……Come to think of it.”
I’ll ask him about whatever comes to mind.
“It seems I actually came to Mirage when I was little, too.”
“Serge, have you heard anything from your grandmother about what happened back then?”
“……No. This is the first I’ve heard of it. Back then, were you with your parents……?”
“I’m pretty sure….”
I search my memories.
“……It was with my father. I think my mother had already passed away by then.”
“……Is that so? ……If I find out anything about what happened back then , I’ll let you know.”
"Please."
As if retracing my memories, I decided to stroll through Mirage.
As you leave the hotel and walk down the bustling street, someone greets you cheerfully.
“Aria! You’re Aria, right? It’s been a while…!”
“[主人公]! You’re [主人公], right? It’s been a while…!”
Of course, I thought it was our first meeting, but...
Staring intently at his face, she suddenly realizes something.
When I was little, Leon wasn’t the only one I met on this island.
“……Could it be that Finn-san is… that Finn-san?”
“When I was little, Leon used to play with me a lot on this island…”
“That’s right! That brings back memories…!”
He smiles, narrowing his eyes happily.
“Since we’ve finally met, if you have time , how about we go sightseeing together?”
“……I’d love to, but I’ve got something else to do today .”
“I see… Well, I guess there’s nothing I can do about it. Let’s talk again when we have time. But more importantly—”
“Just call me ‘Finn,’ okay? And please stop using honorifics.”
“Hehe…”
Finn was supposed to be Leon’s younger brother.
Hearing something similar somehow makes me feel a little warm inside.
I visited the Administration Bureau to meet Ahès.
But...
“……Not home?”
“Aren’t you out somewhere having fun? I’ll be back before sunset.”
“……Do you know roughly where that is?”
“I guess it varies by day, but anyway. I think I see them around the cathedral quite often…”
"Thank you!"
Relying on the information from Yuris, I made my way to the cathedral.
“Hey, can I ask you something?”
Find the children playing and speak to them.
“Do you know that girl, Ahès?”
“I know. Is she your friend, big sis?”
“Yeah. We made plans to hang out the other day, but…”
“I went to the Administration Office, but they weren’t there. Do you know where they are?”
“Hmm… Ahès… if I take my eyes off her for a second, she just wanders off.”
“I have absolutely no idea where I’m going. Sorry, big sis.”
“Hmm. Thanks for letting me know.”
I went around to the back of the cathedral and peeked into the gazebo.
There, you’ll see Evan relaxing on a sofa.
“Hello, Evan. …Have you seen a girl around here?”
“Ah, Ms. Lapraud. Hello.”
“The child… didn’t see it. Maybe they just didn’t notice.”
“I see… Thank you.”
I suddenly wondered about this, so I asked.
“Do you like this gazebo, Evan?”
“Ah… No, what I’m really interested in is Vil’s culture within Mirage.”
“It naturally gives me more opportunities to come here, and since there’s a bench where I can rest, it’s just the right place for deep thought.”
Come to think of it, I feel like he said something like that when we first met, too.
At that moment.
“Ahès!”
When I called out to her, Evan narrowed his eyes as if intrigued by the reason why.

en: “That’s good… Actually, I’ve been looking for you because I have something I want to ask you.”
“……What?”
“Ahès, do you have an older sister? Someone around my age…”
“Why?”
“I feel like I once met a girl on this island who looked a lot like you .”
“……Oh, I see.”
Ahès smiled at my sudden question.
“I don’t have any siblings.”
“I see… Sorry for asking such a weird question.”
“……Hey, Miss Lapraud. Have you been to Mirage before?”
“I didn’t really get that impression, though.”
“Yes… Actually, I remembered it yesterday.”
“It was when I was little, so my detailed memories are a bit vague, though…”
“I suppose that means, ‘As I walked around the island, memories that had been buried in my subconscious resurfaced,’ .”
“That’s quite interesting.”
I smiled ambiguously.
I can’t say that I actually remembered because of the shock of coming into contact with magic.
The next day...
When I went to the restaurant for breakfast, I ran into Leon.
Since I was invited to join them anyway, I sat with them and chatted about things like what I did yesterday.
“How is Leon spending his time here?”
“I’ve got a few business meetings, and I’ve been making the rounds at social events … but I’m here strictly on vacation, after all.”
“To be honest, I wanted to spend yesterday with you, too. If you were going out, I wish you’d told me.”
“I-Is that so?”
Leon continued, lowering his voice slightly.
“……I’m worried, partly because of the original book. From now on, try to invite me along as much as possible.”
“Leon… Thank you.”
That was when it happened.
“Aria. …Rudy asked me to tell you. He wants you to come to Portail Bleu.”
“[主人公]. …Rudy asked me to tell you. He wants you to come to Portail Bleu.”
After breakfast, I headed straight to the Administration Office.
"I have time, so I’ll tag along," says Leon, who is accompanying me again this time.
In the Director’s Office, Rudy and Yuris were waiting for us.
Today, there’s apparently going to be a discussion about the documents found at Grandma’s house and their contents.
After confirming whether it was okay to have Leon present, Rudy immediately got down to business.
“……The island’s secret—since it’s a matter that touches on the very core of it all, I was actually torn about whether I should tell you this.”
“We’re being shown privately owned materials because of our position. Just wanted to let you know.”
As he spoke, his complexion didn’t look too good.
Maybe I’ve been burning the midnight oil reading through the materials for the past few days.
“I haven’t been able to check everything yet, but could you take a look at this for now?”
Leon and I both lean in to look at the book Yuris held out to us.
This book appeared to be my grandmother’s diary.
“……There is a description there regarding an organization called the ‘Platinum Midnight Cult’ .”
He states this in a completely matter-of-fact tone.
“It says that this so-called cult was systematically kidnapping Mirage’s children.”
“Huh…?”
He said it so casually that my mind went completely blank.
“Kidnapping a child…?”
“On this island, children occasionally go missing . It doesn’t happen very often, though….”
“……It’s been going on for decades now. Some of them are even newborn babies.”
“Most of them were thought to be accidents at sea, but…”
“So that was actually a kidnapping, was it? What was the culprit’s motive?”
“Well then. Since there’s no ransom demand, at least it’s probably not for financial gain.”
“……So, you’re saying Grandma knew who the culprit was ?”
“Based on what’s written here. However, I don’t know if what’s written here is true.”
Leon’s expression remains stiff as he thinks in silence.
Eventually, he said, as if muttering to himself.
“……‘The Platinum Midnight Cult,’ huh.”
“……Do you know?”
“It’s a secret society based in London. They hold séances based on spiritualism and raise money.”
“On the surface, it was supposed to be a charitable organization that ran orphanages and such….”
“A few prominent figures I know have joined, but regular members probably don’t know anything about it.”
Yuris replied in a voice laced with exasperation.
“Spiritualism, huh. Well, I guess I can kind of see why someone would want Mirage’s child .”
“……What do you mean?”
“……We talked about this a little while ago, didn’t we? There are many families of sorcerers on this island.”
“Just imagine. No matter how much we prohibit the removal of information about the island—”
“It’s inevitable that rumors will spread about a ‘book that grants any wish’ appearing or a ‘magical island.’”
“And as for magical talent, the vast majority of it comes from one’s bloodline.”
“If they really want to hold a séance, that organization would be desperate for a sorcerer’s blood, wouldn’t they?”
“W-Wait, does that mean…?”
Without meaning to, my voice trembled.
“To that end, the children…”
“Just because I might be able to use magic? For decades…?”
Why……
This is way too bad.
“Why would you go to such lengths…?”
“……It’s to make money by abusing magic, isn’t it? There’s no end to the people who try to take advantage of mages.”
Rudy spits out the words bitterly.
“That’s just too awful…”
“……I feel the same way as you do.”
“Sacrificing children just to make money is absolutely unforgivable.”
“……Or perhaps that sect has a belief system similar to a new religious movement.”
“Faith… Ah. So you worship magic. You brainwash the children you’ve abducted and turn them into priests for your organization? ”
“……No way…….”
It’s too brutal; it doesn’t feel realistic.
“Also, there are a few other documents of interest from the Laplard family’s workshop.”
“It’s about the sea god worshipped on this island— Sirene…”
“――First, let’s talk about the festival.”
“This is a ritual to give thanks to the Sea God, who protects this island and bestows blessings upon its inhabitants.”
“The original text is—her blessing, and a form of grace bestowed in response to human prayers.”
“Aria-chan, that’s what your grandma told you, right?”
“[主人公]-chan, you heard that from Grandma, didn’t you?”
You will be prompted to verify again.
“……It seems your grandmother believed there were two gods on this island.”
“Huh?”
As for Sirene, the goddess who protects Mirage, I’ve heard stories about her here and there, but…
As for the existence of the other deity, no one had mentioned it.
“I’ve only just started looking into this, though…”
“To begin with, I’m skeptical about whether the one currently being worshipped on this island is really Sirène.”
“……Maybe we were actually worshipping something completely different.”
“Didn’t the Administration Bureau notice? I mean, the possibility that they might have mistaken the god?”
“……To be honest, I never even questioned it. I’ve believed it just as I was taught since I was a child.”
“……Well, I guess that’s what tradition is all about.”
Leon gave a wry smile, as if he understood.
“Is that all we’ve learned from the documents?”
Yuris gives a weary, wry smile.
“There are countless others, too… Like magic to relieve back pain, or herbs to improve eyesight.”
"If I were to explain everything, it would take all day, so I’m just giving a brief overview."
“Another thing that seems important is… ‘The Forbidden Art of Finding the Original Book,’ I suppose.”
Finally, when the words were added as an afterthought, I couldn’t help but ask him to repeat them.
“Is there a way to find the original book?”
“It’s impossible under normal circumstances. Since this is a way to force through the impossible, it requires a considerable sacrifice.”
“To put it simply, in order to find the original book, I have to open the path—the path of the spell that connects me to the book— .”
“The moment it connects to the original book, the book’s magical power will flow directly into the mage.”
“Water… moves from high places to low places, right?”
When I learned magic from my grandmother.
I seemed to recall hearing those words before.
“That’s right, that’s right. Look, that’s exactly the phenomenon that happened just the other day at Lapraado’s house.”
“That’s because Grandma didn’t mean any harm —so it ended up being just a minor outburst.”
“The magic of the original book isn’t something a human vessel can fully contain . That’s why the caster’s mortality rate is quite high.”
“……So it’s literally a gamble, is it? There are people out there who are willing to go that far just to get their hands on the original book.”
Rudy nodded solemnly.
“……During the festival period, conflicts arise over the original text. You should be very careful, too.”
“If you find it too much to handle, the Administration Bureau will take it back anytime.”
“……Thank you.”
After finishing our conversation, we left Porte-Bleu.
Leon says with a look of deep resolve.
“……Aria. From now on, I want to spend as much time as possible with you.”
“……[主人公]. From now on, I want to stick with you as much as possible.”
“After hearing Rudy’s story… I became even more worried about you, the one who has the original book.”
“……Thank you, Leon.”
If he’s by my side, I feel like my anxiety would ease a little.
On our way back to the hotel, we ran into a pair with a strange combination.
“Young lady, so you were here…”
“Jack? What’s wrong?”
“This kid said, ‘Please find Aria,’ so I’ve been searching everywhere.”
“This kid said, ‘[主人公], please find it,’ so I was searching all over for it.”
“I don’t really get the hang of this, but even if I refuse, they keep pestering me, so I have no choice but to…”
Jack seemed confused.
Ahès, on the other hand, didn’t seem particularly flustered and appeared calm.
“Aria, help me. I have to go right now.”
“[主人公], Help me. I have to go right now.”
“Huh? Really?”
Faced with this sudden request, I instinctively look at Leon.
He said nothing and just stared back at me.
I felt like they were leaving the decision up to me.
“I’m not really sure… but okay.”
“Where should I go?”
I was brought to the Cathedral of Vil.
I was wondering what was here when—
“Whoa…!?”
Suddenly, a small scream was heard.
By the time I realized that the voice belonged to the child climbing the tree…
The child had been slammed onto the ground.
“Hmm…!”
Jack quickly runs over to the boy.
It seemed a broken branch had pierced him, and within a few seconds, the boy’s clothes had been stained bright red.
It appears he has damaged a major blood vessel; if left as is, he will die in a matter of minutes.
(First aid――)
The moment I thought, “I have to do something about this.”
――The original book appeared right before my eyes.
What should I do? I know the answer.
My instincts still remembered what I had been taught.
“……Activation of the body. Assistance with natural healing.”
Light pours from the original book, enveloping the boy.
“……What’s going on……?”
“I’m not sure about using this right off the bat, but oh well. …That’s just like you.”
While being watched by a bewildered Jack and a wry-smiling Leon —
I am doing my best to treat them.
Fortunately, the wound closed up right away.
I can’t make up for all the blood I’ve lost, but for now, I’d say I’m out of danger.
“That’s amazing, Aria…”
“That’s amazing, [主人公].”
“Thank you……”
At that moment, I suddenly felt something was off.
When I arrived here as requested, a boy had just fallen from a tree and suffered serious injuries.
(It’s as if Ahès knew this would happen from the very beginning…)
I had a feeling something was off, but the moment I blinked , I couldn’t figure out what was wrong anymore.
At that moment.
“Hey, Fräulein.”
I hear a melodious voice and look up.
“So you were chosen for the original book, huh? …If you don’t mind, could we talk for a bit?”
Invited by Charles to have a talk—
After entrusting Ahès and the boy to Jack, Leon and I entered the cathedral.
It’s no longer time for prayer, and there’s no one else but us.
“About that book you were holding earlier. Do you know what that is?”
I couldn’t answer either of those right away.
Because I don’t know how much Charles knows .
Staring at me as I remained silent――
Charles smiled gently.
“Excuse me, Meine Liebe. Let’s start with this first . I should have explained the situation first.”
A serious gleam shone in those eyes.
“I have a wish I absolutely must fulfill. That’s why I came to Mirage.”

“Does that mean they’re willing to go that far just to bring this world to an end?”
“……Hmm. Things aren’t looking good. Xeno already has the original book.”
Jack hesitantly raises his hand.
“I heard the story about the original book granting wishes the other day, so I understand it. But….”
“To begin with, why is that book called the ‘original’ ?”
“Why, you ask….”
“Come to think of it, the original book… so, you mean the original book, right?”
“Strange, isn’t it? Does a manuscript of this even exist?”
Rudy let out a small sigh and said.
“……The meaning of the original text is exactly as it says. It is considered the progenitor of all grimoires in this world.”
“……In other words, to put it simply, the few magical tomes that remain in the world—”
“Does that mean all of these are copies of Mirage’s ‘original book’?”
“I didn’t give you the book just to make you fight.”
“It’s a gift in return for what people have given me.”
“You can use magic even with just one book. If three people join hands, even special wishes can come true.”
“……See? You’re happy, aren’t you?”
(……I think I heard something from someone about the original book ……?)
I concentrate on recalling the vague memory that flashed through my mind as clearly as possible.
……Just then.
Fragmented memories began to flood in.
“……I’m still alive. But I’ve been cursed.”
“I just gave you a reprieve—that’s all. The deadline is when you turn twenty.”
“Are you okay, young lady? …You’re as pale as a ghost.”
He peered at my face as if concerned.
“Huh?”
“I’m… cursed…”
Evan blinked, looking puzzled.
“I… will die when my 20th birthday comes. When July 12th comes…!”
My voice trembles.
Once I start remembering, the fear won’t stop.
“……What’s suddenly wrong? Calm down. You’re not thinking clearly right now.”
“I-It’s true…!”
They stare at me with concern.
But Leon alone remained silent, his expression somber.
Still confused, I...
That’s a relief……
Leon?
“……I’m, I’m sorry. I’ll calm down……”
For now, I decided to take a deep breath.
Even if I speak emotionally, you probably won’t believe me.
My heart is pounding so loudly.
Forcing myself to calm my nerves, just as I was about to open my mouth.
“――It’s the curse of the Evil God.”
“……Leon?”
“Could it be… that you knew something about my curse…?”
He nodded painfully.
“……Ah. ……I’ve been wanting to do something about that curse .”
My heart is pounding so loudly.
Forcing myself to calm my nerves, just as I was about to open my mouth.
“――It’s the curse of the Evil God.”
“……Ahès?”
I wonder when this appeared.
She said that in a whisper.
Evan tilts his head and asks.
“……What do you mean by ‘Evil God’? Is it the same as Xeno’s goal?”
Doesn’t anyone find her presence strange?
The story continues as is.
“……I see. ……There are two deities— —in this sea that the islanders call gods.”
At those words, both Rudy and Yuris seemed caught off guard.
It seems that even the Administration hasn’t been informed of this yet.
“……Gradron, King of Cornuaille, became devoted to the teachings of the new god.”
“To protect her kingdom from the invasion, Princess Dayu built a new capital and evacuated the people.”
“With the help of the fairies, he tried to protect that town like a treasure, cherishing it dearly.”
“……That’s the legend of the chair, isn’t it?”
“It is not uncommon for culture to be rewritten as new religions trample upon indigenous beliefs.”
“It is not uncommon for indigenous gods to be labeled as demons, or for great leaders to be portrayed as tyrannical kings.”
“……Mirage is the wreckage of Isu that sank into the sea. Since ancient times, the islanders have worshipped Dayu.”
“To protect their faith from foreign cultures, they changed their name to Sirene.”
“As a goddess, Sirene bestowed her blessings upon this land and became an object of worship.”
“But… that seat has been taken over by another god.”
“Huh?”
A gasp of surprise escapes her lips.
However, Evan nodded as if he were satisfied.
“……Just as I thought. I did think it was a bit strange, though.”
“Strange…? What do you mean?”
“It’s the fact that ‘Otogirigusa’ is being used in the Cronne dedicated to Sirene.”
“……What’s wrong with that?”
“Do you know another name for Otokiri-gusa? St. John’s Wort, that is…”
“! ……<dic=323>The Baptizer</dic>, huh?”
When you pointed it out, I realized it too.
“Dayu is a native deity and a new faith— an entity that contradicts the teachings of the Church.”
“And yet, weaving the flowers meant to honor the church’s clergy into the crown for her…”
It’s tantamount to betraying her.
“……I wonder where the other pillar that took Sirene’s seat came from?”
“Peace in Isu didn’t last long. The kings—my father and the others—chased us all the way to the capital…”
“I appealed in the name of the king to hand the capital over to the newcomers.”
“The princess, defending the capital all by herself, was utterly exhausted. She was sad. She felt lonely. …It was at that moment.”
“The Red Prince seduced Dayu. ‘Let’s protect what’s precious to you together,’ he said.”
“……And so, the princess took his hand.”
“……Back then, I was still human…… Unable to see that it was evil, I handed over the key to the floodgate.”
“……With its floodgates opened, the City of Is was swallowed up, for the most part, by the depths of the sea……”
“Dayu managed to put him to sleep, and they fell asleep together at the bottom of the sea.”
“So, does that mean there’s another Red Prince?”
Ahès nodded slightly in agreement.
“But his power was stronger than I’d expected…”
“By stealing the faith that should have been offered to Sirene, does that mean he is nearing awakening?”
“I see…”
“……There are many gods throughout the world that devour people.”
“The burning of the palace, the famine that came without warning… Even the sinking of the large mail ship—it was all their fault.”
I gasped.
The United Kingdom’s mail ship—the Titanic.
That maritime accident was a tragedy that was beyond human control.
What if that was the work of the Evil God?
……With a feeling that was neither confusion nor sadness, I felt as if I had a headache.
“It wasn’t that I was angry with people or held a grudge against them. …It’s the same as not noticing the ants at your feet.”
Her words trail off.
The room fell completely silent.
It was Leon who broke the silence.
“……Let me get this straight. So, the one currently enshrined in the cathedral isn’t Sirène, but the other one, right?”
Ahès nodded silently.
“That’s what’s cursing Aria.”
“That’s cursing [主人公].”
“……I see.”
Ahès nodded again.
With the intensity of someone confronting her, Leon says.

en: “……If I gather three copies of the original book and make a wish, her curse will be lifted, right?”
“Yeah. After going through the ritual of collecting the original books, I’ll strengthen Sirène’s power and create a moment when I can surpass him.”
Savoring those words――
Leon spoke with a serious expression, expressing his resolve.
“……Well then, it looks like there’s no way I can hand the original book over to that guy, Xeno, now.”
“To protect the world. And to protect Aria, too.”
“To protect the world. [主人公]—to protect that, too.”
“Leon……”
Charles gave a wry smile and spoke up.
“I was counting on this year’s festival, though. Unfortunately—”
“It would leave a bad taste in my mouth to fulfill my own wish even if it meant letting the Princess die.”
“Charles…”
“Besides, I can’t just ignore Xeno.”
“If the world were to end, that would be inconvenient for me, too. I’d be in trouble if the girls who love me were to disappear.”
Rudy let out a small sigh.
“……I never wanted the original book to begin with. As the Administration Bureau, both now and in the future, I will do what must be done.”
“Xeno, who uses the original book to cause harm, must be stopped.”
“……Well, I suppose so. Saving the world —I don’t think I’m capable of something so grandiose.”
“It doesn’t seem like I can just tell them to ‘do it on their own without dragging me into it’ .”
Jack shrugged his shoulders, but a faint smile played at the corners of his mouth.
“It’s definitely turned into something on a scale that goes way beyond just personal wishes, hasn’t it?”
“……I, for one, find this very intriguing. I’d really like to be included in the group as is.”
“Of course, I’m more than happy to help out generously with knowledge and such.”
“Everyone……”
“Thank you……”
It brings tears to my eyes.
Xeno’s goal is, of course――
I also suddenly remembered my own curse.
I didn’t even know how to face it, but I was just anxious and scared…
“……I’m actually pretty lucky.”
“If everyone lends a hand, I’m sure we’ll manage somehow.”
There are people who will stand by me.
Just that alone was enough to make me believe everything would be fine.
“The problem is the location of the original books. One of the three books is with Aria.”
“The problem is the location of the original book. One of the three books is with [主人公]-chan.”
“And then, there’s another copy that Xeno has. I wonder where the last one is…”
“――No one has it right now.”
I couldn’t help but ask him to repeat the words he had muttered under his breath.
“No one? …Is that even possible?”
“I’ve heard that ownership of the original book is transferred either when the owner clearly expresses the intention to transfer it or by killing the owner …”
“Other than that, you can also relinquish ownership. …To be precise, a transfer to nothing.”
“Is it like a squirrel hiding food?”
“Well, that’s an easy-to-understand metaphor. Though it’s a bit too idyllic for the situation.”
How on earth does Ahès know even that much?
No one ever asks about that.
(……Hmm. Right now, I don’t really have time to worry about such minor details ……)
“……The owner of the third book was involved in an unexpected accident. They didn’t even have time to use the power of the original book.”
“……If that’s the case, does that mean the original book—which belongs to no one—was left beside the body?”
"Right."
Thus, my immediate goal became to find the third original book before Xeno does.
That said, I can’t just half-ass making the crown to display in the cathedral either.
Since we all had our own schedules, we decided to set aside time whenever we could.
After finishing today’s work, we returned to the hotel.
“Hey, Leon….”
I speak to him while waiting for the elevator.
“I just kind of remembered.”
“When I collapsed from the curse… Leon tried to help me, didn’t he?”
“……It took me a while, but let me say this. Thank you.”
“It’s no big deal. If a friend fell down right in front of you, anyone would lend a hand. …Right?”
Is she a little shy?
He smiled awkwardly.
“……It’s blue, isn’t it?”
“So even Leon Vitry is a young man his age, I suppose.”
As someone chimed in from the side, Leon glared discontentedly at Charles and Evan.
“You’re creepy! Don’t come over here…!”
“……If your appearance never changes, that’s not human.”
It’s not good if it stays the same all the time.
In that case, let’s make sure it goes unnoticed.
So that even when I’m there, everyone won’t be scared.
“Wonderful…! Please continue to bestow many blessings upon me!”
They seem happy.
But all I ever hear is, “Do more.”
Having come to take it for granted, they eventually stopped devoting themselves to their faith.
(Oh no...)
Even though I like people.
I just want to be by their side.
I’m feared, shunned, and hated.
……So, make sure no one notices.
I decided to keep a quiet eye on things.
After breakfast, I headed to the reception desk to meet up.
“Good morning.”
Today, I was supposed to go look for the original book with Leon and Charles.
It seems they both have time until after noon.
And then...
For some reason, she was there too.
“Why Ahès?”
“I’ll help you look, too.”
“Is that so…? Thank you…”
“I checked just in case, but it seems no report of a suspicious death has been filed with the Administration Bureau yet.”
“In other words, the body of the original book’s owner still hasn’t been found …”
“There is, in fact, a magic spell that can conceal a corpse. You just have to make sure no one’s attention is drawn to it.”
“Even if a corpse were right in front of me , I wouldn’t be able to recognize it. Conveniently, the stench of decay doesn’t reach me either.”
“However, if a mage attacked, ownership would have transferred, so that possibility is unlikely.”
The story unfolds based on Ahès’s statement that ownership of the original book is up in the air.
(Just a hunch...)
(This feels a little off, though...)
“I see. Well then, assuming it was an accidental death—”
“Shall we take a look, focusing on places out of sight and dangerous areas ?”
First, following Ahès’s guidance, I made my way through Vil’s Forest and went to check out the cliff behind it.
Locations where accidental deaths are likely to occur.
Also, I narrowed my search to places that seemed hard to spot and tried searching with , but...
There was no way the body would be found that easily.
By late afternoon, we had returned to Fleur d’Or Square.
“……If the body fell into the ocean or something , wouldn’t it be impossible to find?”
“I guess we just have to wait for it to wash ashore somewhere. In that case, I wonder if the original book will wash ashore too?”
At that moment.
Finn, who happened to be passing by, called out to me.
“Hey, Leon. Are you with Charles Paradille today?”
“Aria’s got a lot on her plate, but she’s caught in the middle. …Don’t forget my invitation, okay?”
“[主人公] is tough enough as it is, and now I’m stuck in the middle. …Don’t forget my invitation, okay?”
“Since we’ve finally met, if you have time , how about we go sightseeing together?”
“Yeah, sure. When I have some free time—”
Just as I was about to answer that...
Suddenly, that dream flashed through my mind, and I hurriedly corrected myself.
“Uh, excuse me! Do you have time later today? I actually wanted to talk to you about something.”
“If you’d like, how about grabbing a cup of tea somewhere?”
“Ah, uh. Sure, that’s fine… What about those two over there?”
“I have to get back to the theater now. It’s about time for Monsieur Vitré, isn’t it?”
“……Ah. I have one business meeting today.”
“See you later, Haze.”
Saying goodbye to a stern-faced Leon and a smiling Charles, I set off walking with Finn.
I did say it would be fine to do it somewhere more casual, though...
“I’ve been pretty successful, so don’t hold back,” said Finn, as he took me to a wonderful restaurant.
“……Hey, that’s good.”
Seeing Ahès, who had naturally tagged along, Finn looks slightly puzzled.
While I was wondering where to start, the conversation naturally turned to stories from my childhood.
“Do you remember? Picking up seashells, or being taken to a cave near the sea …”
“Yeah. I feel like I actually had quite a few fights with Finn.”
“Ah, she did it! She’s a tough one despite her looks, and deep down, I was completely flustered.”
“Hehe… Is that so?”
We laugh together.
Then, Finn says, as if suddenly remembering something.
“……I’ve even felt a little jealous sometimes because you’re so attached to Leon.”
“So, I lied to Leon and told him I’d left my pocket watch in the cave .”
“Come to think of it, maybe I just wanted it to be just the two of us on the way home.”
“But in the end, you chased after Leon and went back to the cave…”
“……That was my first heartbreak, wasn’t it?”
And then, upon returning to the cave—the mausoleum—I ended up being cursed.
Finn has absolutely no idea about any of that.
But if I knew…
I’m sure I’ll end up feeling responsible.
Now that I had regained my memory, it was easy to imagine that.
I take a deep breath, then look at Finn again.
“……Hey, Finn. What does the Flores Trading Company mean to you?”
He blinked, looking slightly surprised.
“……Did I mention the guild’s name? Well, it’s a symbol of my independence. Or rather, something precious that I want to protect……”
“If someone tries to destroy it, what would Finn do?”
“……Of course, I’ll fight.”
“Even if that person is important to Finn?”
Finn stared at me as I continued to ask unrelated questions, then fell silent.
Staring at him as he looked bewildered, I spoke up.
“Finn, do you know about the Platinum Deep Night Cult?”
A faint sense of tension ran through me as I spoke that name.
“I met that leader. …He’s trying to bring an end to this world.”
“The world? …No way, that’s ridiculous.”
"That’s impossible," he said with a wry smile.
It seems people think this is just a pipe dream.
“It’s true, you know.”
At Ahès’s words, a frown lines his brow.
……If that dream isn’t just a dream.
Finn may be cooperating out of goodwill, unaware of Xeno’s true intentions.
“……I don’t think there’s any need to fight someone I don’t want to fight.”
“But I thought that if I broke something important without realizing it, I’d surely regret it…”
Finn remained silent, saying nothing.
I’m sure everyone has their own thoughts on this, but personally, I’d prefer it if you could step away from this matter.
I don’t want to fight my childhood friend, whom I’ve finally managed to remember.
Besides, I thought he, too, surely didn’t want to bring about the end of the world.
After leaving the restaurant, Ahès and I walk home as dusk falls.
“……I wonder if Finn got the message.”
“I think it’s okay.”
“If you’re worried, just use magic. It’s that easy—easy enough to change a person’s heart.”
She said that without any ill intent.
“……No. I’m not going to do that.”
Magic is a terrifying thing.
It was scary to think that such power could touch people’s hearts.
(? What’s that…?)
Leon and Mei were together.
Of course, Percy is also waiting in the wings.
Was Leon’s errand to meet her?

en: “Leon, Ms. Mei.”
“Oh, Aria.”
“Oh, [主人公].”
“What were you talking about?”
“Just a little small talk. Don’t worry about it.”
Now that you mention it, I’m even more concerned, though…
It would be rude to probe too deeply, so I didn’t go any further.
――I can hear the adults’ voices.
“I guess the vessel couldn’t take it…”
“The ritual failed. I only intended to transfer the magical power, but it became permanent.”
“The boundaries of consciousness are being eroded. That’s just a ghoul now. It’s useless.”
……Who is this “Ghoul” referring to?
“No, it’d be a shame to kill him. If I seal his magical power, he’ll temporarily return to human form.”
“From now on, try as much as possible not to let it use magic. If its magical power increases, it might run amok.”
“Even if I let him live, it’s impossible to completely sever ties, isn’t it? Is there any point in going to all this trouble?”
“There’s a use for it as a ghoul.”
“Monsters that kill people are actually quite useful, after all.”
“Another weird dream…”
Could this be caused by a hallucination as well?
If what I’m seeing now is something that happened in the past…
I thought it was a cruel tragedy.
Today, the three of us—Rudy, Jack, and I—had planned to go look for the original book.
As expected, Ahès was also at the meeting spot this morning.
I’m really happy you’re helping out, but it feels kind of strange.
I’m sure I didn’t tell her the time we were supposed to meet.
“Forests, well, there are just so many accidental deaths in them… Depending on the situation, you can even get lost in a small forest near a village.”
“……Be very careful not to stray from the path. If you slip, there’s no telling how far you’ll fall.”
Push open the door of the abandoned church.
There were various items scattered about, but there didn’t seem to be anyone around.
When you step outside the abandoned church—
Rudy and Jack seemed to have sensed something; I felt the atmosphere had changed.
The next moment.
Suddenly, the ground beneath my feet gives way slightly.
“Whoa…!”
Jack catches me and Ahès, who were about to fall into the hole, and pulls us toward him.
――Then, stones rained down on us like bullets.
“Huh!”
With a rapier he’d pulled from somewhere, Rudy slashed at the air.
Immediately afterward, a strong wind swirled up, shielding us from the projectiles.
“Ugh…”
A bitter-sounding click of the tongue can be heard from somewhere not too far away.
Looking closely, I could see a figure emerging from among the trees.
(This person……)
He is a young man named William, who had requested interviews with Charles and Leon.
And then...
That name also belongs to the boy who appeared in my dream.
“Even though that person warned me, I’m still trying to find out more.”
“There’s no way I’d survive that…!”
He glares at us with eyes full of murderous intent.
“It’s just perfect—Jack’s even here!”
“Huh…?”
Just as I instinctively tried to look over at Jack...
Once again, the ground beneath his feet collapses due to magic.
Just as he lost his footing and lost his balance, another stone flew at him.
But Rudy sharply slices through the air, using the Wind of Magic to protect us.
"Damn it……!"
William grits his teeth in frustration.
As if aiming for that very moment—
Jack raises his gun with a practiced motion and fires.
“Huh!?”
The bullet struck Mr. William’s leg precisely.
“……Do you know who I am?”
Jack casts a wary glance at the bleeding young man.
He seems to have absolutely no idea what Mr. William was referring to earlier.
A voice filled with rage echoes through the forest.
“As if I know anything…! Because of you, look what we’ve been put through…!”
His expression contorts with resentment and pain.
“――I’m going to kill every last one of you!”
Immediately after William barked.
“Ugh…?”
Suddenly, he clutched his chest.
“Ah, ugh…? —Gaaah!?”
After a moment of confusion, a cry of anguish rises.
I could sense the magical power within him swelling and spiraling out of control.
William’s form begins to transform into a beast-like, monstrous creature unlike anything he has ever seen.
“W-What is that…?”
“Could it be… a ghoul…?”
Jack fired his gun again, as if to keep the enemy at bay.
At the same time, Rudy also swings his rapier and unleashes a gust of wind.
If they were human, they would have certainly taken an attack that wouldn’t have gone unpunished.
He—the ghoul—remained standing on his own two feet.
“……Aren’t you going to kill me?”
“That’s not human anymore, you know.”
“! Ahès……”
When asked with a puzzled look, I—
I want to help
I’d like to hear your thoughts.
“……I won’t kill you. If I can, I want to help you.”
What distinguishes humans from everything else?
I don’t know.
But...
“……First, I need to hear what they have to say.”
He must know something.
Also...
Something I saw in a dream had been weighing on my mind.
“……I see.”
“Are you satisfied?” Ahès replied briefly and nodded.
(……How can I turn the Ghoul back into Mr. William ?)
Most likely, he is currently unable to control his magical power.
Then, if I can just stop it from running amok—
Things might calm down temporarily.
“Rudy, Jack!”
Pick up the original book and speak to the two of them.
“Can’t you stop the ghoul? Just for a little while.”
A look of confusion flashed across their faces.
……But that only lasts a moment.
He nodded as if he had made up his mind.
“……I understand.”
“I’m not confident, but I’ll give it my best shot.”
Without any further discussion, they sprang into action.
Rudy generates a shockwave with his rapier, startling William.
Next, Jack aimed for his knee and shot through it.
“Gah!”
“――Stop!”
The moment he spoke those words, a flood of light engulfed him.
He growls as if resisting.
“Hmm…!”
I focused my mind, determined not to lose.
As if to suppress the rampaging magical power with my own magic, drawn from the original text.
For several seconds, the clash of magical energies continued――
When the light subsided.
……As if the mask were being torn away.
The body, which had been distorted and swollen by magic, shrank and regained its human form.
Without a sound, he collapsed right there on the spot.
“Ugh….”
He had been unconscious, and when he awoke, it was around sunset.
“……W-what is this……?”
Did you realize that you were bound by magic and couldn’t move your body?
He looked up at me in surprise.
“This is Porteau Bleu. This is the Administration Office.”
In this parlor, besides Mr. William, there are only me and Ahès.
I thought people might say this was dangerous, but...
When Ahès asked, Rudy immediately gave his permission.
He muttered, sounding confused.
I will convey the facts frankly.
“There is a ghoul inside you.”
He let out a gasp, as if caught off guard.
It seems even the fact that I myself have undergone a transformation is still unclear.
“I suppose I underwent a ritual when I was little. …Don’t you remember?”
At first, he was dumbfounded.
But...
Did a memory come to mind?
Before your very eyes, they lose their color, and their eyes are gradually stained with despair.
Ahès said he isn’t human anymore, but…

en: “I think the ghoul inside you is reacting to magical power and becoming active.”
“So… um, I think it would be better if you didn’t use magic anymore .”
……If I just suddenly told you this, you might not believe me.
I conveyed that while thinking that, but...
Did something finally click?
“……There’s no way that’s possible……”
He never voiced his suspicions; instead, he spat out a refusal.
“Without magic, I’m useless…!”
“……Even though you’ve been turned into a ghoul, do you still want to be useful?”
“Hmm…!”
He gasped as if startled.
Xeno may not have been involved in the events from William’s childhood.
But...
The fact remains that the Cult turned him into a ghoul.
“……I don’t think we need to work for people like that . ……At least, I don’t.”
“Don’t let outsiders say whatever they want! I’ve always lived for the Cult…!”
Flustered, his voice trembled with emotion.
“Besides, unlike him, I was treated with care!”
“What do you expect me to do now?! Are you telling me to survive on my own?! There’s no way I can do that!”
I can’t say I don’t understand the desire for unchanging protection.
William’s concerns are entirely justified.
“……I think it’s hard to live on your own. But—”
“If you keep using magic like this, …you might not be able to go back.”
I’m sure he knows it himself.
If he keeps repeating that, his sense of self will soon be completely swallowed up by the ghoul.
“It’s okay. As long as I’m alive, I’ll manage somehow.”
“Mr. William, you really should just become a newspaper reporter or whatever— .”
I tried to say it cheerfully.
“If you’re from the United Kingdom, you can speak English as well as the Republic’s language, right?”
“You could aim to become an interpreter or a language teacher…”
“It’s okay to start from scratch and figure out what you want to do. On your own.”
If I were in his shoes, I’m sure I’d be afraid of the future.
But...
If he stays where he is now, before long, he will no longer be him.
……If you don’t like that, you have no choice but to move forward.
While I was stringing together optimistic words...
He said nothing and fell silent.
Mr. William was deemed to require restraint, supervision, and above all, protection—
At least until the festival ends, the Administration Bureau will take custody of him.
Today, it’s Charles, Evan, and me. And then…
The four members of Ahès, now a familiar group, continued their search for the original book.
“Come to think of it… A few days ago, I saw a traveler heading into the forest.”
“! What kind of person was he/she?”
“They’re well-dressed men and women, so I wondered if they were going for a walk in the woods or something.”
“Did you see where I came back from?”
“No. I had work to do, so I couldn’t go that far.”
“I see… Thank you.”
We thank her and part ways with the woman on the island.
“That’s the most reliable information we’ve had so far.”
Charles smiles gently and says,
“That said, perhaps I simply took an elegant stroll through the forest and returned to the hotel without incident.”
“It’s not entirely impossible that he/she got lost in the forest and tragically lost his/her life .”

Are you interested in going to the theater? He seems enthusiastic about it.

The stage is so close that I can’t help but get excited by the view—one that can’t be seen from the regular audience seats.

Ahès and I leaned forward, enjoying *The Nutcracker*.
After the show.

Charles interrupts his mid-sentence.

While watching the tide, take a look around several spots, such as near the pier.

Maybe...

Next, just as Xeno draws a line in the air, trace the air with your fingertip.

Is the wound quite deep? He couldn’t stand and collapsed onto the sandy beach.

Hand over the original book

Cannot be transferred.

After his mutter, his magical power grows even stronger.
Before we even had a chance to resist or try to escape, it swallowed us all whole—

……He fell pitifully onto the sandy beach and rolled around.

en: “Rather than having a ritual performed on you without your consent in an unfamiliar place, wouldn’t it be better to be prepared?”

“Yuris, is….”

Before we knew it, Ahès was walking right beside us.
“Believe it or not, I’m actually quite devout… Every morning and evening, I pray at the Great Temple.”

“I’m keeping an eye on you, too.”

To think that young Ahès would be taking an interest in the adult Yuris.
The childlike way of speaking is endearing.
Because I handed over the key to the floodgate.
Because I succumbed to the clumsy devil’s temptation, the City of Is was swallowed by the sea.
……The ruins of the town, which I desperately protected so as not to lose a single piece.
Mirage.
This island, itself.
Together with the man who attacked Isu, I fell asleep at the bottom of the sea, and many long years have passed……
The power of people’s prayers—by gathering their faith, I became so great that I came to be called God.
However, when the islanders began to seek the god’s blessings more fervently.
They misjudged their opponent.
(I had a strange dream...)
……This vision felt somehow different from the ones I’d had before.
Feeling a strange sense of unease, I sit up in bed.
Over the past three days.
We combed through every nook and cranny of the places where Xeno might be hiding.
But I still haven’t gained anything in particular.
Today, I must once again pour my heart and soul into searching for Xeno and crafting Cronne.

I was planning to talk about something today.

“……I feel like words alone won’t be enough to stop Xeno.”
However, I don’t have the original book with me right now.
“To protect myself and everyone else, I wanted even the slightest means to do so…”

But when something I thought could never happen in reality happens right before my eyes—
Even though things are like this, it feels like a dream.
“I see. I understand the gist of it now.”
The teachers—Charles and Rudy—nodded in agreement.
“Monsieur Vitré truly has no aptitude for magic.”
“T-That much…?”
“Jack seems to have the knowledge, but he’s just not cut out for this, is he?”
“Evan… as expected, you’re quick to grasp the logic. But for now, I don’t know if it’ll actually work.”
“That’s a shame… I was hoping there might be some hidden talent lying dormant.”
Evan looks, as the saying goes, a little frustrated.
Jack asks, looking interested.
“So, what about you, young lady?”

“Of course, it’s not something that can be done in just a day or two. Don’t even think about trying to fight Xenon with magic.”
“……I understand.”
Rudy thought for a moment, then said to me.
“……I think you’re probably compatible with water.”
“Let’s master the principle of creating water from thin air and how to manipulate water that already exists in the area.”
"Yes!"
At that moment.
Suddenly, Jack exhaled.
“……What if magic were something more convenient?”
“I bet I can easily find the place where Xeno is hiding, .”
“Magic isn’t just magic. There are rules and limitations. It’s a far cry from the miraculous power that makes anything possible. ”
“Come to think of it….”
“She was creating tools to help anyone use magic easily.”
“I heard from Serge that my grandmother was good at making magical artifacts.”

Given the number of people, the room—which isn’t very spacious to begin with —feels even smaller.
“……Aria. ……What is this……?”
“……[主人公]. ……What is this……?”

As soon as he saw what Ahès had found, Evan let out a gasp of surprise.
It was a glossy, jet-black object, shaped like a plate.

As he touched his fingertip to the mirror, Charles tilted his head .
